“If only I had bought Bitcoin back then...”

“I knew NVIDIA was going somewhere. Why didn’t I invest?”

Everyone has thought about it at least once.

But what if you could actually go back?

It is the year 2030. After losing your job to AI, you struggle to get through each day with little hope for the future.

Then a home AI robot named Honey Dragon (H.D.) appears and offers you a second chance:

Return to 2010—and seize the investment opportunity of a lifetime.

Trade and Live Through History

Money Makes Money: Historical Market Simulator takes you through the markets of 2010–2025.

Search for companies, study charts, read historical news, and trade stocks and cryptocurrencies before advancing to the next month.

Invest in companies before they reshape the world. Enter the cryptocurrency market before it becomes mainstream. Prepare for the crashes, recoveries, and opportunities that history has already revealed.

Knowing the future does not make every decision easy.

Living costs continue to accumulate, unexpected events demand money.

God gave you two crucifix pistols. Use them to shoot your way out of hell. Four arenas, four bosses, and a lot of things in between that want you dead. Think you can make it out?

Every shot you land fills your momentum meter. The higher it climbs the quicker you run, the more you dash, the harder you hit. Take one hit and you lose all of it.


GODSPEED was created entirely by one person, including all the 2d/3d art, programming, sound, and music.

store_data.about_the_game:
STORY

Is it an urban legend, a mystery... or something else?

— One day in August, 2026 —

You become a paranormal influencer and head to the remote region of Kirigasawa in pursuit of fame and fortune—a place rumored to have swallowed up several influencers who vanished while filming there.

When you step off the bus, you're greeted by a beautiful sea of trees surrounded by towering mountains.

Beautiful, that is... except for the ominous signs.

Eager to begin filming, you soon discover your first destination—a ruined hospital—and eagerly make your way toward it.

Suddenly, you lose consciousness.
When you finally open your eyes again...

You're inside a hospital straight out of 1970s Japan—and it's no longer a ruin!

Then, your phone begins to ring...
Even though you should have no signal.

SYSTEM

Four different endings await, including the True End.

Is it an urban legend, a mystery... or something else?

— One day in August, 2026 —

You become a paranormal influencer and head to the remote region of Kirigasawa in pursuit of fame and fortune—a place rumored to have swallowed up several influencers who vanished while filming there.

When you step off the bus, you're greeted by a beautiful sea of trees surrounded by towering mountains.

Beautiful, that is... except for the ominous signs.

Eager to begin filming, you soon discover your first destination—a ruined hospital—and eagerly make your way toward it.

Suddenly, you lose consciousness.
When you finally open your eyes again...

You're inside a hospital straight out of 1970s Japan—and it's no longer a ruin!

Then, your phone begins to ring...
Even though you should have no signal.

store_data.about_the_game:
Meowing is the only way to find them. And the only way to be found.

Your three kittens are lost somewhere in the forest. You are small, you cannot fight, and something is hunting them by sound.

Call out, and a kitten answers — but so does the thing in the grass.

A predator that hears you

A black panther prowls the forest. It never sees you first; it hears you. Every meow, every footstep, every second spent out in the open is a decision. Learn its breathing, its steps, the moment the birds go quiet.

Blind in the grass

The camera sits low, at a cat's eye level. Tall grass hides you completely — and hides everything else. Climb onto a stump to see over it, and you become the most visible thing in the field.

The light is running out 

Each run begins at golden hour and ends in the dark. The longer you take, the less you can see — and the closer it gets to your den.

Carry them home

One kitten at a time. Slower, louder, unable to crouch. The last trip home is always the worst one.

Short runs, different every time

Six to twelve minutes. Kittens hide in different places, the panther comes from somewhere new. Every kitten you bring home stays home — even if you don't make it back.

store_data.about_the_game:
BUILD THE COMIC SHOP OF YOUR DREAMS

Comic Shop Tycoon is a first person shop management simulator where you start with a small comic book store and work to turn it into a successful business.

Order new inventory, unpack deliveries, stock your shelves, set your prices, ring up customers, and put your profits back into the store. Each day gives you another chance to improve the shop, bring in more products, and grow your business.

RUN YOUR SHOP YOUR WAY

You take care of the day to day work yourself. Keep your shelves stocked, clean up the store, manage incoming deliveries, work the register, and make sure your customers can find something they want to buy.

STOCK MORE THAN COMICS

As your store grows, so does the selection of products you can sell. Along with comic books, you can carry collectibles, figures, tabletop RPG books, dice, comic supplies, and other merchandise.

KEEP UP WITH NEW RELEASES

New comics arrive over time, so you will need to plan ahead, order what you need, and make room on your shelves. Keeping popular products in stock can make a big difference when customers come through the door.

GROW YOUR BUSINESS

Earn money and experience by running the store. Unlock new products, expand your available space, improve your shop, and keep working toward something bigger.

MAKE THE STORE YOURS

Decorate and customize your comic shop with posters, standees, fixtures, murals, and other items. Build a store that feels like your own and give customers a place they will want to come back to.

BUILD YOUR COMIC SHOP EMPIRE

Start small, learn the business, and build your store into the kind of comic shop you would want to visit yourself.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your power is in the cards you can't draw.

Every creature card belongs to a strain. Play one and it doesn't hit for the number printed on it — it hits for the entire population of that strain, everywhere in your deck at once. Draw pile, discard, hand, all of it counts. You never need to find the right card. You only need it to exist.

Every card asks the same question, every turn.

HARVEST it for damage now, or SOW it to breed more of its strain and hit harder for the rest of the run. There is no energy bar. Your hand refills to five and every card in it is yours to spend — the cost of sowing is simply the damage you chose not to deal. Greed has an axis: go deep on one strain for a multiplier that collapses all at once, or go wide for something steady that never spikes.

Carrying capacity is the ceiling. Going over it is how you get ammunition.

Every strain has its own cap. Cross it and breeding stalls, the end of each turn spits Feral cards into your deck, and if two strains are over at once the larger one eats the smaller. Feral cards are dead weight you cannot play. They are also the only fuel for BLOOM.

BLOOM is a bomb you build out of your own mistakes.

Six Feral cards arm it, and a permanent gauge shows exactly what detonating deals and what it costs you — so it is never a random punishment. Hold at eighteen and it goes off on its own. Every turn you wait makes the bomb bigger, the recoil worse and your hand deader. Set it off and every strain collapses back to its cap; you rebuild from half a colony.

The enemies watch what you are breeding, and they leave you a tell.

Nineteen of them, every attack telegraphed two turns ahead with a condition written underneath it. Meet the condition before you end your turn and the blow lands light. The check reads your colony at the moment you stop — so the forecast is never only "how much is this going to hurt," it is "what am I allowed to do this turn."

Every run runs on different physics.

You sign a Contract before you pick a single strain, and it rewrites the rules for the whole run — one restriction and one compensation, never just "harder this time." Drought crushes every cap but breeds you an extra creature. Bare Hands takes PRUNE away entirely. Monoculture gives you one strain instead of two, then makes it enormous. Choke doubles your overflow and lets you detonate twice as early.

The run ends on a sheet worth posting.

Win or die, you get a Herbarium specimen page: the strains you raised, the mutations that drifted into them, your peak population, your Blooms, the Contract you signed. Ten strains, three visible growth stages each, six heritable mutations — the colony you finish with is not one anybody else has had.

Features

  • 25–40 minute runs — five layers, and a boss announced on the very first screen: The Gardener, The Glasshouse or The Seedsman
  • Ten strains with three growth stages each, nineteen enemies, six heritable mutations that drift as your colony breeds
  • Six Contracts that change the run's physics; eleven post-battle nodes with five on offer every time
  • Five verbs and no bloat — HARVEST, SOW, BURN, PRUNE, DETONATE. You never do multiplication; every card previews its own result on hover
  • A screenshot-ready Herbarium sheet at the end of every run, win or lose

store_data.about_the_game:
THE MARKET IS A CASINO.

Wheel Street is a single-player financial roguelike deckbuilder played on a circular board. Read the week ahead, manipulate your assets, and assemble strategy-card combos that turn every market swing into increasingly absurd returns.

READ THE MARKET BEFORE IT MOVES

At the beginning of each week, the full five-day market outlook is revealed.

Land on an asset during an up day to cash in its current value. Hit it during a down day to double its value for the future. The market is not hiding anything from you—the challenge is arranging the board so that you are always in the right place at the right time.

Grow during the downturn. Cash out during the rise.

CONTROL THE BOARD

Each day, choose from three movement cards. Use one to move your pawn clockwise around the board, or spend your cards to reposition the assets themselves.

Move assets into empty spaces, merge matching sectors to combine their value, or swap different assets to reshape the board. Every position affects what you pass, where you land, and which effects will trigger.

Luck determines your options. You decide how to exploit them.

BUILD YOUR PORTFOLIO

Collect assets from technology, crypto, consumer goods, commodities, real estate, and banking.

Concentrate assets from the same sector to activate unique abilities, including dividends, sector rotation, leverage, futures, location bonuses, and compound interest.

Then add strategy cards that bend the rules of growth and settlement. Combine their conditions, control their trigger order, and create profitable chain reactions.

INVEST OR CASH OUT?

Your wallet is both your score and your spending power.

Investing in new assets can make your portfolio stronger, but every purchase also takes money away from your current weekly target. Decide when to reinvest, when to save, and when to push your luck for one more explosive payout.

Meet the target to advance, earn tokens, and visit the shop. Fall short, and the run is over.

EVERY RUN IS A NEW MARKET

Randomized starting assets, market patterns, card choices, and shop offerings turn every run into a new strategic puzzle.

Build around the opportunities you are given, discover unexpected combinations, and see how far your portfolio can climb before the market finally catches up with you.

  • Circular-board movement and asset positioning

  • Roguelike card and portfolio building

  • Fully visible market cycles

  • Six asset sectors with unique synergies

  • Strategy-card combos and chain reactions

  • Escalating weekly cash targets

  • Randomized runs with high replayability

No investment experience required. Terrible financial instincts welcome.

store_data.about_the_game:
ONE TOWER. ENDLESS WAVES.

You get a single tower at the centre of the arena. Everything else is a decision about where the money goes.

Every wave you clear pays out immediately, and you spend it mid-run: damage, attack speed, crit chance, crit factor. Six weapon mounts fire at once — Tesla coil, mortar, beam laser, flak cannon, ricochet shredder, railgun — and each has its own upgrade lines. Run ends, cash converts, and the permanent side of the game opens up.

THE CONSTELLATION

453 passive nodes across six arms and six keystones. Points come from your progression level, not from clearing an arbitrary wave, so the tree is open from early on and keeps paying out for hundreds of runs. Sockets take jewels that rewrite what the nodes around them do.

BUILT AS A PREMIUM GAME

No ads. No timers. No energy bars. No currency sold for real money. You buy it once and the whole game is there.

WHAT'S IN IT

14 weapons, 6 simultaneous mounts, 10 sectors of escalating difficulty, a 453-node passive tree, jewel sockets and attunement, 64 achievements, offline earnings, and a workshop of permanent upgrades that raise where every future run begins.

store_data.about_the_game:
A failed energy experiment split the world into five unstable regions. Vikings now cross frozen oceans, mutants roam the ruins, machines guard an abandoned citadel, and creatures emerge from a place where the laws of physics no longer work.

You lead Aegis Division, a team sent to recover five Quantum Cores and rebuild the Eclipser Engine. To reach them, you will need to fight through 100 stages and defeat the boss controlling each region.

BUILD YOUR TEAM

Choose heroes from five classes: Tank, Sniper, RPG, Medic, and Tactician. Each class has a different role, so a strong team needs more than raw damage.

Place durable heroes on the front line, protect weaker units in the back, and adjust your formation to deal with different enemy teams. You can save formations and reuse them in later battles.

FIGHT YOUR WAY

Battles are turn-based. You can choose basic attacks, skills, ultimates, and targets manually. Skills consume energy, powerful abilities have cooldowns, and attack speed helps decide turn order.

If you would rather focus on building your team, turn on auto-battle. Your heroes will choose their actions and targets automatically, and you can return to manual control when needed.

UPGRADE AND EXPERIMENT

Heroes grow stronger as they level up and unlock new skills. Equip class-specific gear, upgrade abilities, collect buffs, and use shards to forge new heroes, gear, and upgrades.

Buffs can provide shields, healing, critical bonuses, armor penetration, reflection, camouflage, status effects, and other advantages. Different combinations may work better against different enemies.

EXPLORE FIVE REGIONS

The campaign takes you through the Frozen Dominion, Mutant Wastes, Infernal Depths, Cyborg Citadel, and Void Frontier. Each region has its own enemies and boss.

Recover every Quantum Core and decide what happens to the fractured world.

FEATURES

• Turn-based battles with optional auto-battle

• Five hero classes

• Manual control of attacks, skills, ultimates, and targets

• Front- and back-line formation building

• Hero levels and skill upgrades

• Gear, buffs, forging, and team progression

• 100 single-player campaign stages

• Five regions with different enemies and bosses

• English, Japanese, and Arabic interface support

Buffs can provide shields, healing, critical bonuses, armor penetration, reflection, camouflage, status effects, and other advantages. Different combinations may work better against different enemies.

The campaign takes you through the Frozen Dominion, Mutant Wastes, Infernal Depths, Cyborg Citadel, and Void Frontier. Each region has its own enemies and boss.

Recover every Quantum Core and decide what happens to the fractured world.

• Turn-based battles with optional auto-battle

• Five hero classes

• Manual control of attacks, skills, ultimates, and targets

• Front- and back-line formation building

• Hero levels and skill upgrades

• Gear, buffs, forging, and team progression

• 100 single-player campaign stages

• Five regions with different enemies and bosses

• English, Japanese, and Arabic interface support

store_data.about_the_game:
Good Meat is a 16-bit console inspired incremental game about two brothers who hunt and cook meat to serve to their customers and earn money. Help them build their business from a wooden food cart in an alleyway to a galaxy-sized empire capable of purchasing entire planets!

Hunt For Meat!

Control Jeff the Hunter in an exciting, arcade-y, top-down shootout with cute, snuggly animals. Click them to death to earn raw meat: the lifeblood of your restaurant business. Over time you will become stronger, gain powers, and strike fear into the hearts of the universe’s fauna across many different biomes!

Feed Your Customers!

Chef Jordan delivers delicious meat straight into the face of his hungry customers in an automated JRPG-battle-styled cooking session. Help him by selecting his special moves, increasing his power through Quick Time Events, and picking up his precious tips. Unlock new special moves and employees who will join your party to assist you, all in the name of feeding everyone ever. Yes, Chef!

Build Your Empire!

For the Bartolo brothers and their empire, vertical integration is the name of the game. Earning coins from your customers allows you to purchase real estate to upgrade your restaurant. Each building you purchase upgrades the brothers, their business, or their employees. Purchase enough buildings and you can leave the city for the world and beyond! Expand your empire with the greatest weapon ever created: Capitalism!

16-bit Meat Puns!

Inspired by the 16-bit console generation, the Good Meat world is MARBLED with humor and nods to classic games to sate that appetite for nostalgia. Rise up to MEAT the challenge! Don’t be a CHICKEN! The STEAKS have never been higher! Conquer the universe for a job WELL-DONE!

Take charge of Japan's national volleyball team. Select and develop players, then lead your team into international competition.

store_data.about_the_game:
Same alley, same night, never the same danger

You're trapped in a cramped, dimly lit alley that winds past old houses, rusted iron gates, and tangled power lines. There's only one way out — light all 10 candles.

But every time the loop resets, only one candle stays lit. The rest, you'll have to find and light yourself. And in the dark... you're not alone.

Whatever lurks in the alley follows its own rules

The anomalies haunting this alley don't hunt you at random — each one follows a specific rule you'll have to learn the hard way. Some can't be looked at. Some wait for the moment you move at the wrong time. Some hide in whispers that sound a little too familiar. Survival here means paying attention, trusting your instincts, and being willing to die and learn — because death in this alley is the best teacher you'll get.

The deeper you go, the darker it gets

Early loops might only bring a single shadow to watch for. But as you close in on loop 10, the alley fills with overlapping anomalies at once. You'll need to remember every rule, for every threat, and decide fast — before the last candle goes out for good.

🕯️ Loop-Based Horror System — Light all 10 candles across 10 increasingly difficult loops. Die, and you start over — but what you've learned stays with you.

👻 Diverse Anomalies, Each With Its Own Rule — No universal strategy. Every threat demands close observation and memory.

🏚️ An Alley You'll Come to Know By Heart — Weathered houses, iron-barred doors, tangled wiring, and faded shop signs, all rendered in painstaking detail until it feels like a real place you've walked before.

🔦 Light Is Your Only Friend — Sometimes — Knowing when to use it, and when to disappear into the dark, is half the battle.

🎧 Listen Closely — Not Everything You Hear Should Be Trusted — Whispers, footsteps, music. In this alley, sound itself can be a trap.

😱 Escalating Pressure With Every Loop — When multiple anomalies appear at once, you'll have to prioritize fast, in the dark, with panic setting in.

store_data.about_the_game:
She was the only one who could read it. Now she's dead, and it's still running.

A rune-tape program runs the pressure ward that keeps the Drifted City aloft. It ran correctly for eleven years. Last night it killed the engineer who maintained it.

You have her listing. Her logs. Her stepper.

Find the instruction that did it.

You never write a line of code. You read one.

Faultfinder is a deduction game with a debugger for a magnifying glass. Every case opens as three panes: her annotated listing on the left, the machine's live state in the middle, and on the right what the city actually observed. A pressure reading that held at zero for nine seconds. A door that reported closed while it stood open.

Your tools are a debugger's, not a programmer's:

  • Step one instruction and watch exactly one thing change.

  • Break on a line, or on a condition: stop when PRESSURE drops below four.

  • Watch a register and read its whole history as a strip beside the tape.

  • Rewind. The entire trace is recorded. The scrub bar runs both ways.

  • Inject a different reading from the outside world and re-run it. Some faults only wake for one input in a thousand.

Then you commit. Name one line. Name one fault from a fixed vocabulary: off-by-one boundary, uninitialised register, wrong branch polarity, overwritten value, unit mismatch, missing bounds check. Then name the moment the harm was done. Get all three right and the report writes itself, one clause at a time.

Every case has exactly one answer. That is not a promise. It is a proof.

Faultfinder's cases aren't designed and playtested into fairness. They're machine-verified before they ship. Each one is built by taking a correct program, applying a single seeded fault, and then proving by exhaustive simulation across the whole input space that the faulty program fails, that reverting that one instruction fixes it, and that no other single change can.

If a case has a second defensible answer, the pipeline rejects it and you never see it. No designer ever adjudicates whether your reasoning was fair. The machine already did.

The program is a character document.

M. VOSK kept this ward for eleven years. She annotated her own tape in pencil, translating each rune for herself in her first year, because nobody had taught her either.

Her glosses thin as the cases go on. Her comments get terser. There is a line she commented out, years ago, with the note leave this.

You are the first person in eleven years to read her carefully. You are eleven years late.

For the specific pleasure almost no game has dramatised

If you have ever written software, you know the feeling of a bug collapsing into obviousness. The moment a mess becomes a sentence. Faultfinder makes that collapse the win condition and puts a body underneath it.

And if you haven't: you don't need to. Nothing here asks you to author anything. The blank page is the wall that keeps most players out of programming games, and this game does not have one. Her handwritten gloss sits beside every rune in the first case. Hover translates anything, always. No case is ever gated on remembering.

In the demo

  • Seven cases, 35 to 70 minutes, on one machine: the pressure ward on the city's underside

  • A fourteen-instruction rune-tape, taught by using it

  • Six classes of fault, each hiding in a different way

  • Full rewind, conditional breakpoints, register watches and input injection

  • Her story, told entirely in marginalia and log fragments

Wishlist Faultfinder to hear when the full ward opens.

From Endpaper

A solo studio in Somerset. Built in Godot.

store_data.about_the_game:
Once, your family stood among the wealthiest merchant houses in the world. Your name carried influence, your warehouses overflowed with goods, and your fortune seemed as vast as the seas themselves.

Then catastrophe struck.

In a short time, everything your family had built was lost. Properties were seized, investments collapsed, and every reserve of wealth disappeared. Desperate to survive, your family borrowed from friends, rivals, moneylenders, and anyone willing to offer even the smallest amount of help. But the debt only continued to grow. With nothing left to sell and nowhere else to turn, you did the only thing you could think of.

You prayed.

Perhaps you had accumulated some merit in a previous life. Perhaps the gods simply took pity on you. Whatever the reason, your prayer was answered, and you were granted one wish:

A way out of your hopeless situation.

Unfortunately, divine mercy has its limits. There was no mountain of gold waiting for you. No miraculous cancellation of your debts. No forgotten inheritance. The gods gave you only one thing:

"A SHIP"

At first, you could hardly believe it. How could a ship possibly solve the enormous debt hanging over your family? The divine answer was simple:

“No one can help those who refuse to try.”

The world is vast, divided by seas and oceans, filled with cities producing different goods and markets where the same commodities command vastly different prices. A ship may not be a fortune, but it is enough to travel. Enough to carry goods. Enough to seek opportunity.

And perhaps, enough to begin again.

Naturally, your first idea is to sell the ship. Unfortunately, once you compare the value of the vessel against your family’s mountain of debt, the truth becomes painfully obvious. Selling it would barely make a difference. You might survive for a short while, but eventually the creditors would return, and you would be exactly where you started. So there is only one reasonable choice left.

Use the ship.

Gather whatever meager wealth remains. Sail from city to city. Buy commodities where they are cheap and sell them where they are valuable. Study the markets, discover profitable routes, endure losses, take risks, and slowly rebuild the fortune your family once possessed. But the world of commerce is never predictable. Prices rise and fall. Yesterday’s profitable commodity may become tomorrow’s disaster. A forgotten market may suddenly offer an extraordinary opportunity. Every voyage takes time, every purchase carries risk, and every decision brings you either closer to freedom—or deeper into debt.

You were not given salvation. You were given a chance.

A ship, a little money, an enormous debt, and an entire world waiting beyond the horizon. And in this world, there is one truth understood by every man of wealth:

Fortunes are not simply found. They are made through trade.

Kings may rule, nobles may inherit, but those who rise by their own hands do so as merchants—buying, selling, taking risks, and turning opportunity into wealth. If you are to rebuild your family name, there is only one path left before you.

"TRADE"

store_data.about_the_game:
HYPERSCALE is an idle data centre builder where the servers were never the hard part. Alone in a shed on somebody's back paddock, your job is to turn one rack into a campus that lights up the horizon. Ten sites stand between you and hyperscale. Can you keep the lights on?

MIND THE FREQUENCY

Fifty Hertz or Nothing: Supply and demand have to match every second of every day. Build compute faster than you build generation and frequency sags, and the grid starts dropping your racks to save itself. Get it wrong badly enough and it takes the whole site with it.

Nothing Runs Without It!

Click to dispatch: and get the megawatts up. Grid, diesel, solar, wind, batteries, and eventually things that need their own fence (think nuclear!). Every brown option of them is cheap and hated (but so fast), or dear and tolerated green options (better for skippy). Pick your poison.

RUN THE COMPUTE

store_data.about_the_game:
Paver: Tidy Up Together is a satisfying first-person organizing game where you sort and place pavers to rebuild a plaza. Work at your own pace, follow the correct patterns, unlock useful skills, and watch a chaotic area gradually transform into a perfectly restored plaza.

Game Modes

Play solo or together in online co-op.

  • Normal Mode: Progress normally and unlock new skills as you play.

  • Sandbox Mode: Jump straight in with all the skills unlocked. 

  • No-Skill Mode: Challenge yourself with all skills disabled and complete the layout manually.

Paver Layout Plan

The restoration of the old castle is nearly complete—but the grand plaza is still unfinished. During the renovation, all pavers are mixed across the ground. Fortunately, you have the original paver layout plan. Your task is to place 4,064 pavers in the correct places. There are pavers with different colors, and also different shapes like rectangle, square, octagon, trapezoid, H-shaped, triangle, hexagon, trihex, and radial.

Skills

  • Highlighting Paver Layout: Highlights the correct place for the topmost paver in your hand

  • Auto-Placement: Automatically places your pavers in the correct places

  • Auto-Collect: Automatically collects the same pavers as the topmost paver in your hand

store_data.about_the_game:
The Freshest Meat in Town

Dead & Delicious is a first-person co-op simulator about running a burger joint during a zombie outbreak. Out front, customers are waiting for their order. Out back, the horde is coming. You'll be doing both jobs at once, and you'll be doing them badly. That's the fun part.

Two Jobs, One Counter

Customers and zombies show up at the same time. Someone has to take the order. Someone has to hold the back door. Nobody has time for either. Balancing the register and the shotgun is the entire game, and it falls apart in the best possible way.

Fresh Cuts

Pistols, shotguns, katanas and other close-range tools are all on the menu. Zombies come apart where you hit them: shoot the head clean off, take a leg with a blade and watch it drag itself toward you anyway. Every kill is a physics-driven mess, and every mess is an ingredient.

From the Back Door to the Bun

Haul the pieces inside and load up the meat grinder. Crank the handle, pack the meat, and drop a fresh patty on the grill. Cook it right, stack the burger, hand it over. Simple work, if the shop weren't actively being overrun.

Upgrade the Joint

Spend what you earn on better gear and a better shop. Improve your equipment, expand your setup and make each shift a little less impossible than the last.

Ragdoll Everything

Nothing in this restaurant stands up straight. Your character wobbles as you run, zombies flop when they drop, and one well-aimed object from a teammate will put you on the floor mid-order. Physics is the co-chef, and it is not on your side.

1-4 Players, Online or Solo

Play alone or bring up to three friends online. There are no assigned roles, no classes and no forced jobs. Anyone can cook, anyone can shoot, and figuring out who does what is up to you.

Key Features

Co-op for 1-4 players - play solo or online with friends

Cook and fight at the same time - customers and zombies arrive together

Location-based dismemberment - heads, arms and legs come off where you hit

Firearms and melee - pistols, shotguns, katanas and more

Full meat pipeline - grind the pieces, form the patty, grill it, serve it

Shop and gear upgrades - spend your earnings to survive the next shift

Ragdoll physics everywhere - on the zombies, on the food, on you

Stylized first-person visuals - cartoony, colorful and deeply unserious

content_descriptors.notes:
Dead & Delicious contains frequent cartoon violence and gore in a stylized, non-realistic art style.

Players use firearms and melee weapons against zombies. Enemies can be dismembered, and heads, arms and legs can be severed and detached depending on where they are hit. This is accompanied by stylized blood effects and exaggerated ragdoll physics. Dismembered enemies may continue to move toward the player.

The core premise of the game involves processing the remains of zombies into food. Players carry body parts to a meat grinder, turn them into patties, cook them and serve them to customers who are unaware of what the food is made from. This is presented as dark comedy and is played entirely for humor.

The game does not contain sexual content, nudity, or depictions of self-harm. It does not contain the use of drugs or alcohol. Enemies are undead, not living human characters.

store_data.about_the_game:
Found is a narrative adventure game full of stories, puzzles, and a chance to rebuild a fragmented world. 

Explore a dreamlike soft-poly world that's been torn apart. As Em, a cloaked wanderer with glowing eyes, you'll uncover lost memories, wander through landscapes rich with puzzles, battle unfriendly creatures, and piece the world back together one fragment at a time.

Reassemble a world broken apart

Explore the world to collect fragments that can be pieced together to construct a map that's completely unique to your playthrough. As the world becomes whole, new places, people, puzzles, stories, and sidequests emerge, allowing you to gradually shape both the world and your journey through it.


Explore a world designed for discovery

Discover more than 200 unique levels and the stories and puzzles that tie them together. Unlock new abilities and revisit familiar places from new perspectives.

Discover unforgettable characters

Meet characters and cultures of all types, each with their own quirks and takes on what's happened to the world around them.

Grow your abilities

Manipulate the world by exploding walls, growing plants, disappearing from sight, and lighting the darkness. Combine what you've learned to uncover new places and pieces of the past.

Battle curious creatures

To progress through the landscapes of Found, you'll need to battle the enemies that rose up during the fragmentation. Boss battles are as much a test of your thinking as they are of fighting skills.

Uncover a familiar past

Recover memories and histories scattered across the world to understand who you are and to uncover the events that led to the Fragmentation.

store_data.about_the_game:
🚗 Two Drivers, One Ride, Total Co-Dependency

Are you ready to share control of the same RC car with your friend? If your answer is "yes," you're either incredibly brave or you have no idea what you've signed up for. In WheelMate, driving isn't a one-person job. One of you controls the front wheels while the other handles the rear. And trust us, these two roles are nothing alike!

The front wheels turn gently but pack the lion's share of the engine's power. The rear wheels, on the other hand, pivot like crazy but lack the muscle. In short: one driver uses brute force to punch the gas, while the other frantically screams, "Where are we going?!"

🏗️ The Rogue Tower Crane

The massive tower crane at the construction site has gone entirely out of control! It's spinning endlessly, threatening everything around it, and the site has already been evacuated. Until the crane is shut down, the area will never be safe again. The only thing that can stop it? Your tiny RC car.

Navigate the construction site, reach the tower, and shut down the crane. The mission sounds simple on paper. But in practice, both players need to be on the exact same wavelength. Flawless teamwork is an absolute must. Long story short: You'll either sync up perfectly, or you'll get really good at yelling at each other.

🦀 Lord of the Crabs

This is where the real fun of WheelMate begins. The independent movement of the front and rear wheels turns this from a standard RC car into a completely unique vehicle with unmatched mobility (assuming the drivers are actually capable, of course).

Turn both sets of wheels in the same direction to scuttle along like a crab, or turn them in opposite directions to pull off impossibly tight spins. This mechanic will be your greatest ally as you navigate narrow paths, treacherous drops, and challenging platforming sections. Though, fair warning: it won't be easy.

🎮 Succeed Together, or Crash Together

In WheelMate, the real question isn't who the better driver is—it's who the worse one is. Because that's exactly what you'll be arguing about for the entire game!

Sometimes your friend will scream "RIGHT!" and you'll do the exact opposite. Sometimes you'll overcome seemingly impossible obstacles with flawless coordination. And sometimes, a tiny mistake will send your car flipping right into a brick wall. But those who overcome all these odds and complete the mission will prove that they aren't just "good drivers"—they are a truly spectacular team.

store_data.about_the_game:
When the dead cross the River Lethe, every memory of the life they lived is washed away.

But those memories are not gone.

When a new soul stands trial, the memories of those who knew them in life—and crossed the river before them—rise to the surface.

Those they loved.
Those they hated.
Those who were mere acquaintances.

Within those memories remain parts of the accused's life they never chose to reveal.

The dead who stand trial in the Underworld must recount the life they have lived and defend themselves in their own words.

“I lived a virtuous life.”
“I had no other choice.”
“I am not guilty.”

However, a trial cannot be decided on testimony alone.

You are Dikaion.

You are able to see the memories that rise from the River Lethe.

Look beyond the accused's testimony. Piece together what truly happened through the memories left behind, and prove their guilt before the gods.

But your duty does not end with uncovering their guilt.

You must reveal the true weight of that guilt and argue for the judgment it deserves.

That is the role of Dikaion.

Three judges await in the court of the dead.

They weigh the accused's testimony based upon the memories you uncover, determine the weight of their guilt, and decide the fate of their soul.

It began like all the others.

The accused recounted his life, and the memories appeared one after another.

His guilt seemed clear.

Only the verdict remained.

Then, just before judgment was passed, one of the judges spoke.

“Wait.”

.

.

With that single word, a trial that should have ended begins again.

As the trial resumes, the truth the accused had kept hidden begins to arise piece by piece.

And it overturns everything you thought had already been decided.

His guilt had seemed undeniable.

Until a truth emerged that could change the verdict.

Once every truth has been brought to light, the final decision is yours.

Your choice will lead this trial to one of two different endings.

  • Reconstruct events from fragments of memory.

How many people were there?
Who was present?
What happened—and in what order?

Connect the fragments of memory that can prove the accused's guilt, then match the right people and actions to the water of recollection to conclude the case.

  • Look beyond the accused's testimony. Uncover their guilt, and prove its weight.

Use the memories left behind by the dead to uncover the wrongdoing the accused chose not to reveal, then present the reconstructed memories as evidence to show the three judges the true weight of that guilt.

  • The final judgment is yours.

Even after every truth has been revealed, there may be no single right answer.

Make your final decision and reach one of two different endings.

.

.

Reconstruct the memories.

Prove their guilt.

And decide.
store_data.detailed_description:
When the dead cross the River Lethe, every memory of the life they lived is washed away.

But those memories are not gone.

When a new soul stands trial, the memories of those who knew them in life—and crossed the river before them—rise to the surface.

Those they loved.
Those they hated.
Those who were mere acquaintances.

Within those memories remain parts of the accused's life they never chose to reveal.

The dead who stand trial in the Underworld must recount the life they have lived and defend themselves in their own words.

“I lived a virtuous life.”
“I had no other choice.”
“I am not guilty.”

However, a trial cannot be decided on testimony alone.

You are Dikaion.

You are able to see the memories that rise from the River Lethe.

Look beyond the accused's testimony. Piece together what truly happened through the memories left behind, and prove their guilt before the gods.

But your duty does not end with uncovering their guilt.

You must reveal the true weight of that guilt and argue for the judgment it deserves.

That is the role of Dikaion.

Three judges await in the court of the dead.

They weigh the accused's testimony based upon the memories you uncover, determine the weight of their guilt, and decide the fate of their soul.

It began like all the others.

The accused recounted his life, and the memories appeared one after another.

His guilt seemed clear.

Only the verdict remained.

Then, just before judgment was passed, one of the judges spoke.

“Wait.”

.

.

With that single word, a trial that should have ended begins again.

As the trial resumes, the truth the accused had kept hidden begins to arise piece by piece.

And it overturns everything you thought had already been decided.

His guilt had seemed undeniable.

Until a truth emerged that could change the verdict.

Once every truth has been brought to light, the final decision is yours.

Your choice will lead this trial to one of two different endings.

  • Reconstruct events from fragments of memory.

How many people were there?
Who was present?
What happened—and in what order?

Connect the fragments of memory that can prove the accused's guilt, then match the right people and actions to the water of recollection to conclude the case.

  • Look beyond the accused's testimony. Uncover their guilt, and prove its weight.

Use the memories left behind by the dead to uncover the wrongdoing the accused chose not to reveal, then present the reconstructed memories as evidence to show the three judges the true weight of that guilt.

  • The final judgment is yours.

Even after every truth has been revealed, there may be no single right answer.

Make your final decision and reach one of two different endings.

.

.

Reconstruct the memories.

Prove their guilt.

And decide.
store_data.short_description: The River Lethe holds memories of the dead. Use its memories to uncover what happened and prove a soul's guilt in the Underworld. His guilt seemed clear—until truth shook the verdict. Knowing all the truth, can you still call him guilty? A story-driven psychological horror about memory and judgment.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Night Shift

Uncle Frank's food truck is yours now. The plan seems easy: work the night shift, keep the grill hot and feed the outcasts wandering the night. But you’ll soon realize people at your window aren't looking for a normal meal. They’re bringing their deepest traumas and darkest secrets to your counter.

Read Between the Lines

Forget standard menus. Instead of asking for a simple burger, your patrons speak in strange riddles driven by emotions and sensory cravings. Listen to their unusual rants and figure out which ingredients on your station actually match their hidden confessions. Your deduction skills are your best tool to satisfy their hunger. Every bite is a confession, and the grill is your interrogation room.

A Sinking Feeling

As the nights drag on, the line between a bad job and a living nightmare starts to blur. The grill is yours. Stack curious, unconventional ingredients however you want to build the perfect dish. Satisfy your patrons, uncover the truth behind Uncle Frank's legacy, and remember: the customer is always right, no matter what they ask for.

store_data.about_the_game:
Prof. Bobo, who is the chief scientist at the Dream Making Lab, has vanished. Tamanegi learns of his disappearance while on vacation. It seems like a strange group called "Moon Coffee Cult" is behind it. As he rushes to his help, he will go through fantastic spaces like the museum where the children hide, a crystal forest... and many more fantastic landscapes. Where can he find his beloved Prof and brew the antidote together?

No combat. No timers. No losing. Just engaging conversation, observation, and simple puzzles. A short, mysterious adventure full of challenges and cute humour.

A quirky hand-painted point-and-click adventure, with picture book-like, stiff and a little clumsy animations. 

Main Features
- A world painted by hand. Most scenes feature original acrylic paintings on paper, assembled digitally. 
- More than 25 hand-painted based original backgrounds, from a walled town at night to a crystal forest and a tower on the moon.
- Plenty of text-based interaction and props. Newspaper clippings, scattered notes, and many more strange items.
- 15 simple and beautiful puzzles that grow out of the world around them.
- Around 30 characters to talk to: allies, obstacles, and townsfolk with something to say. 
- Playtime: 1–1.5 hours
- Full English and Japanese support (Text)

store_data.about_the_game:
The Velvet Bean has two faces

Your aunt Margot left you a cafe you visited exactly twice. Her lawyer smiled when he slid the keys across the desk, and the last line of her letter reads: "Ask Selene about the Ledger. When she trusts you."

By day the Velvet Bean is an ordinary third-wave coffee bar. On Friday and Saturday nights it becomes something else entirely — the place this city's femboy and futa regulars come to stop performing. The thing that built that second identity was Margot's Velvet Ledger, and the Ledger is missing.

You have forty-five days. Aurea, the chain empire across the block, holds an option on your lease that comes due on the last one. Keep the cafe standing and pay it, or hand Margot's life over to the woman who has been circling it since the funeral.

Six people worth staying open for

Selene, 34. Head barista, and the spine of the place. Dominant, dry, hides her warmth behind needling. She was Margot's right hand, and she does not intend to lose this cafe twice.

Lulu, 21. Pastry chef. Shy, sweet, happiest behind the oven. His family doesn't know who he is; here, he doesn't have to explain.

Coco, 23. Server. Loud, flirtatious, permanently attached to his phone and determined to make the cafe go viral. He's a completely different person once the camera is off.

Nova, 26. Night-shift barista and the door's quiet gatekeeper. Gothic, sparing with words. She used to be Aurea's star, and she is not ready to talk about why she left.

Roxy, 25. Weekend DJ and the architect of the cafe's night identity. Insolent, playful, allergic to rules. He never gives anyone a second night.

Valentina, 31. Aurea's owner. Elegant, arrogant, dangerously easy to look at. She is the reason you may lose everything. She is also the only other person who ever loved Margot.

Run the cafe, then close it and see who stays

Every day runs on the same rhythm and none of them play out the same way.

Morning. Set the menu, invest in decor, and put two people on shift. Money is made and spent here.

Day. Work the shift you staffed. Coffee Rush and Night Mixer are short, generous skill games; performance sets your takings and warms the people you worked beside.

Evening. Choose one person to spend your free hours with. This is where the routes move.

Night. Twice a week the second face comes out: masquerades, karaoke, latte-art duels, a neon picnic, and a Silent Night that belongs entirely to Nova.

The management layer is deliberately forgiving. This is a visual novel with a cafe attached, not a spreadsheet with a romance attached.

Three acts, forty-five days, eight endings

The Velvet Ledger returns one page at a time, and the last page rewrites everything you thought this fight was about. Six full romance routes run alongside it, each with its own crisis to survive — a video that spreads the way Coco never wanted, a secret of Nova's that detonates in the middle of a shift, the wall Roxy puts up the moment anything starts to feel permanent.

Save the cafe and the ending is yours to choose: any of the six character endings you qualified for, or the "Family" ending if what you built here was never about romance. Fail the Midnight Festival and you get the ending you earned instead.

Features

Around 12 hours across 45 in-game days and three acts 6 romanceable adults, 5 relationship stages each 9 themed night events and the two-night Midnight Festival 8 endings, including a fully non-romantic route 12 illustrated adult scenes, unlocked through the story and saved to a gallery Two skill games, a five-tier cafe you visibly rebuild, and a silent nameable protagonist Full controller support with native Steam Input — remap anything from the Steam configurator

About the adult content

Every character in this game is an adult, aged 21 to 34, and each one's age is established in the text. Every intimate scene is consensual, established in dialogue, and takes place between the protagonist and one other character.

WHAT IS THIS

A situation card appears on everyone's screen. You have 15 seconds to choose a video meme from your hand — the one that answers it best, or the one that's so wrong it's perfect.

Then everyone watches all the answers, one by one. Then everyone votes anonymously. Then someone can't stop laughing.

HOW A ROUND WORKS

- A situation appears — 15 seconds on the clock

- Each player picks a video meme from their hand

- All chosen memes play back, one after another

- Everyone votes for the best answer, anonymously

- Points are counted, a new round begins

NO TWO GAMES ARE THE SAME

The same situation hits differently depending on who's at the table and what's in their hand. The joke isn't in the card — it's in the room.

Choose the match length: 10, 20 or 30 situations.

THE ROOM

A dark room. A round table. Pendant lamps overhead. Screens showing whatever someone just decided was the right answer.

FOR 3-6 PLAYERS

Play from anywhere in the world. Get together online, talk with built-in voice chat, and laugh like you're all sitting at the same table.

BEFORE YOU BUY

At launch, all content is in Russian — situation cards and interface. English support is planned. Steam Workshop support is on the roadmap, so you'll be able to add your own memes and situations.

store_data.about_the_game:
Start Broken, Scale Infinitely.

Nozile is a minimal, hyper-fast hack-and-slash roguelike built around high-speed decision making and explosive power scaling. No slow ramp-ups—jump straight into the fray with a fully active kit and push your build past its limits in intense 5-minute runs.

Key Features:

  • Dual-Style Combat: Select 2 distinct fighting styles and swap between them seamlessly in real time to adapt to relentless waves of enemies.

  • Direct Stat Absorption: Defeated foes drop Stat Orbs directly onto the battlefield. Absorb them instantly to trigger aggressive, real-time stat inflation.

  • Fatal Hit System: Chain strikes, shatter enemy defenses, and unleash screen-clearing Fatal Hits to turn the tide in seconds.

  • Pure Build Synergy: Experiment with overlapping armor perks, extreme attack speeds, and custom loadouts designed to break the game's balance wide open.

  • Zero Downtime: Fast loops engineered for quick, highly replayable sessions. Jump in, execute your theorycrafting, and obliterate the horde.

store_data.about_the_game:
The adventurers have been robbing shopkeepers their whole lives. Tonight, you're behind the counter and they're the ones trying to talk you down.

Twilight Tavern is a cozy first-person shop sim about the six hours between 8 PM and 2 AM. Light the door lantern, open up, and see who wanders in.

EVERY CUSTOMER IS A NEGOTIATION

When a customer asks for something, you negotiate price and they answer. Ask too much and they counter. Push further and they walk away.

Three kinds of buyer sit across the counter from you, and each haggles differently.

  • The Cheap Buyer lowballs you at whatever you ask.

  • The Rich Impatient Buyer might just say yes or meet you at their limit and go no further.

  • The Suspicious Buyer negotiates hard and pays in coin you should probably look at twice.

You get two or three attempts per customer. Spend them well.

LEARN WHO WALKS THROUGH THE DOOR

Fifteen named regulars across ten hand-built species:

  • grim reapers

  • vampires

  • witches

  • ghosts

  • goblin peddlers

  • a drifting jellyfish

  • a hopping mushroom monk

  • a snail who takes his time.

They come back, and the shop remembers

MAKE IT YOURSELF

Order stock from Moss & Moon Wholesale, or forage ingredients from Thornwick and craft the things nobody else sells like:

  • Moonroot Salve

  • Starfire Elixir

  • Warding Charms

  • Dragonfire Lamp.

Six recipes unlock as you grow, and the later ones need the earlier ones.

Regulars will commission work directly: craft it, shelve it, and they return the next night to collect at the price you agreed.

RUN IT WITH YOUR HANDS

This is a shop you physically work. Carry products from the backroom.

Slot them onto shelves.

When a customer buys something, walk over, take it off the shelf, and hand it across the counter yourself.

Buy bigger shelves, rearrange them, and fill the room with rugs, barrels, an armchair, etc.

Name the place whatever you like.

SOME COINS ARE FAKE

Sell to the wrong customer and the payment turns worthless.

You lose revenue and your product to a scammer.

Tip: Watch out for what they say, you are the judge of character

One Block To A Billion

One world, 1,006,632,960 blocks and your goal is to take your crew and mine every one of them.

Seven Miner Classes

Hire seven classes of miner: Digger, Brawlers, Colossi, Sprinter, Demolition, Prospector and Colossus. Each has unique stats, a distinct purpose, and its own visual style.

Explore and Find Upgrades

Some upgrades aren't for sale, they're buried. Dig one up and your whole crew gets it.

Boss Fight

Bosses are grown into the bedrock, and they wake when you strike them. Hire Warden Hunters to hunt them down.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE THE LAST TURRET

The enemy walks one road. You are standing on that road.

Gold drops off the enemies mid-wave, and that same gold builds your turrets. There is no build phase and no combat phase. There is one phase, and not enough time in it.

SHOOT

  • Six firearms, pistol to rocket launcher, and a four-step melee ladder.

  • Dash, jump, bullet time. A reload at the wrong moment costs you the base.

  • 30 enemy types: shielded ones that ignore ranged fire, fliers, regenerators, brood mothers.

BUILD

  • Nine turrets - gatling, mortar, tesla, cryo, flamethrower, harpoon and more.

  • Upgrade on the move: walk up to one and hold the key.

  • A turret placed five metres too far back is a lost wave.

SURVIVE

  • 50 missions across five chapters, and nine planetary anomalies: meteor showers, EMP storms, radiation, winds that push your bullets off course.

  • One upgrade card per level. Some of them change the rules, not the numbers.

  • Fourteen skills - carpet bombing, EMP pulse, mines, a jump straight back to base.

store_data.about_the_game:
Layer. Blend. Matching colors disappear.

Place colored pieces onto the board. Red, blue and yellow blend into purple, green and orange; all three together make black, and white lightens whatever it touches. Layer the same color again and that component cancels out and vanishes. Match every cell of the target pattern to clear the puzzle.

Exactly one solution — always

Every puzzle is generated backwards from a finished board, and its uniqueness is verified by an exhaustive count. You will never stumble onto an accidental second answer.

1000 puzzles, graded by depth — not by color count

Four tiers — Easy (4x4, three colors), Normal, Hard and Oni — with the piece count stepping up inside each tier. Adding more colors does not make a puzzle harder; only how many pieces stack on a single color does. That structure is the difficulty curve.

Only the good boards made the cut

Far more puzzles were generated than shipped, then ranked by "small color clumps, many distinct colors" and taken from the top. The selection exists for one reason: so that neighboring cells blend into many different colors.

Built to sit well in the hand

Play with mouse or keyboard. Each of the twelve actions takes up to two key bindings, and the wheel swaps pieces. The board is drawn like layered sheets of colored washi paper.

store_data.about_the_game:
Red is a seasoned thief who infiltrates the last flying island to steal its core. But the heist goes wrong, and Red crashes into the island's lower levels. Now he must make his way all the way to the top, overcoming countless obstacles and uncovering the island's secrets!

Chasing the Sky is a story-driven metroidvania about becoming a hero – and the choices that shape our fate. As Red explores the island, it becomes clear that a terrible disaster has struck. Nearly all of its inhabitants have either turned into monsters or lost their minds. As Red meets the survivors and uncovers the secrets of this place, his view of his mission begins to change. Eventually, he must make a choice: take the core and doom the world, or gather a team and save the island.

Explore crystal caverns, cities in the sky, and deadly fungal forests. Fight monsters and uncover the ancient mystery of the flying island!

Features

  • Grow stronger by unlocking powerful new abilities and skills! Expand your arsenal and become stronger and faster.

  • Discover ancient jewels! Each one holds a mysterious power. Choose the ones that suit you best and make your journey truly your own!

  • Take on challenging trials and uncover the island's many secrets to earn upgrades that will help you on your journey!

  • A huge cast of characters is brought to life through traditional frame-by-frame 2D animation.

If you love classic gameplay, epic adventures, hand-drawn art, and beautiful worlds, Chasing the Sky is waiting for you!

store_data.about_the_game:
The mining colony has ore. The bugs have an appetite.

You have an orbital station, an irresponsible quantity of firepower and one simple order: keep the colony off the menu.

Build towers. Call strikes. Burn the sky. Survive swarms of billions of bugs in a tower defense built around huge battles, persistent progression and increasingly excessive solutions.

The only good bug is a dead bug.

Would you like to know more?

BILLIONS OF BUGS. GIVE OR TAKE.

Workers flood the battlefield. Armored grunts smash through kill zones. Darts skitter past your defenses. Spitters attack from range. Skyrays ignore your carefully prepared ground defenses. Colossi refuse to die. Queens arrive to ruin everybody’s day. Kings mean it's over.

Fortunately, you have guns.

Lots of guns.

Build during the calm, then watch the swarm pour across the map. Reinforce chokepoints, replace destroyed positions and adapt before the next wave turns your perfect defense into a cautionary tale.

DEFEND THE COLONY TOGETHER

Play solo or bring up to three fellow citizens into 2–4 player Steam co-op.

Host a friends-only or public lobby, invite through Steam or jump into Quick Match. Fight together across campaign battlefields, custom maps and subscribed Workshop creations.

Share the battlefield. Split the spoils. Bring your own unlocks. Try not to blame each other when the eastern wall collapses.

A FULL CAMPAIGN

Fight through 26 handcrafted battlefields, each with its own paths, chokepoints and tactical problems.

Every map is a new defensive puzzle. Seal the outpost, unlock the next deployment and push deeper into a campaign where the bugs grow meaner and your arsenal grows much, much louder.

INFINITE PROCEDURAL DEPLOYMENTS

Enter SURGE for a newly generated battlefield every run.

Random layouts, changing nest positions and unpredictable geometry force you to build a fresh defense instead of repeating the same winning pattern forever.

The war continues for as long as you do.

BUILD YOUR OWN BATTLEFIELDS

Open the built-in map editor and paint the warzone yourself.

Create walls, carve paths, position nests, test routes and build anything from a carefully balanced challenge to an absolute tactical nightmare.

Save your creations locally, publish them to Steam Workshop and subscribe to maps built by other players. Then defend them alone or bring them into co-op.

EIGHT TOWERS. SEVEN WAYS TO RUIN A BUG’S DAY.

Build an arsenal of:

  • Gatling turrets

  • Acid sprayers

  • Plasma cannons

  • Cryo towers

  • Sniper emplacements

  • Mortars

  • Tesla towers

  • Flame turrets

Then call in the heavy equipment:

  • Orbital strikes

  • Napalm

  • Cryo-EMP

  • Acid rain

  • Ion storms

  • Gravity wells

  • Bait drops

When the chokepoint fails, remember: you still have the high ground.

The very, very high ground.

A MASSIVE UPGRADE TREE

Every deployment strengthens the next.

Harvest ore, earn gems and advance through 165 persistent upgrades covering towers, orbital powers and prestige bonuses.

Unlock new weapons. Specialize each tower through multiple upgrade paths. Improve your starting economy, reinforce your defenses and turn yesterday’s desperate last stand into tomorrow’s routine pest control.

Lost the run?

The bugs may have won the battle, but they still funded your upgrade budget.

KNOW YOUR ENEMY

The Bug Index tracks seven enemy species, their armor, their behavior and the towers best suited to killing them.

Learn what flies, what spits, what charges and what simply refuses to stop moving.

Then build the correct counter.

Or use more napalm.

Both are valid strategic doctrines.

AROUND 60 HOURS OF MUSIC

Defend humanity to a colossal 986-track soundtrack spanning roughly 60 hours.

Skip tracks, control the volume or let the soundtrack carry you through a campaign, a co-op deployment or one more procedural run that definitely will not last until sunrise.

DO YOUR PART

  • Solo play and 2–4 player Steam co-op

  • 26-map campaign

  • Infinite procedural SURGE deployments

  • Built-in map editor

  • Steam Workshop publishing and subscriptions

  • Swarms of billions of bugs

  • 8 towers and 7 active abilities

  • 165 persistent upgrades

  • Gem-powered prestige progression

  • Bug Index with enemy counters

  • Roughly 60 hours of music

  • One mining colony with an extremely serious pest problem

Place turrets.

Call strikes.

Kill bugs.

Service guarantees citizenship!

store_data.about_the_game:
EVERY SHOT COMES DUE

Bullet Debt is a minimalist arcade arena shooter built on a single rule: your bullets never disappear.

Every projectile you fire keeps travelling. It bounces off walls, off obstacles, off the armour plating of enemies, forever, until it finally hits something. Miss a shot and it doesn't vanish. It becomes a problem you now have to live with, crossing the arena, waiting to come back around. Fire carelessly and the room fills with your own mistakes.

LEARN THE GEOMETRY

There are no random spreads and no wasted shots, only angles. Reflections are mathematically exact, so a bank shot you plan is a bank shot you get. Read the walls, thread a round through a gap, and kill something on the far side of the arena you cannot even see.

Four enemy types, none of which fire back. Chasers come straight at you. Chargers wind up, telegraph, and commit to a lethal dash. Splitters break into two faster fragments the moment you hit them. Reflectors armour three sides and bounce your shots away, so you have to work around to the exposed face.

Special surfaces change your rounds mid-flight. Boosters accelerate them, dampers weaken them, splitters fork one shot into two, and absorbers are the only thing in the arena that will ever clean up after you.

FIFTY LEVELS

A handcrafted arcade campaign of fifty ninety-second levels, unlocking in sequence. Difficulty comes from geometry, enemy combinations and surface interactions rather than inflated health bars. Line-of-sight shadows hide what is behind cover, so threats arrive from where you are not looking. Plus an Endless mode that runs until you die, with a score and a survival time to chase.

LOCAL VERSUS FOR 2 TO 4 PLAYERS

This is where the game really lives. Shared screen, whole arena visible at all times. No split screen, no fog, nobody gets hidden information. You can see every round in play, including the one about to ruin your day.

Score is a timed match with respawns where eliminations pay out and the highest score wins. Stock gives each player a fixed number of lives, last one standing. Rounds is a best-of series with starting positions rotating each round so nobody keeps a favorable corner. Flip enemies on for PvPvE and fight each other while the arena fights all of you.

Turn friendly fire off and switch on limited, recoverable ammunition. Five rounds each, and the only way to reload is to hit your opponent or physically catch your own ricochet out of the air. It gets stupid fast.

A RECORD BOOK FOR YOUR COUCH

Make a profile for everyone who plays. The game keeps a proper sports record: wins, losses, streaks, accuracy, eliminations, damage dealt, favorite arena, and a head-to-head history between every pair of players. Who beat who, how often, and who is currently on a run.

Then run a season. Round robin, single elimination for up to eight players, or a league with a standings table and scheduled fixtures. It all saves, so a rivalry can last for months.

FEATURES

50 campaign levels and 15 dedicated multiplayer arenas.
Local versus for 2 to 4 players, PvP and PvPvE.
Score, Stock and Rounds rulesets.
Persistent player profiles with lifetime stats and head-to-head records.
Round robin, elimination and league tournaments.
Endless mode with score and survival leaderboards.
Full controller support. The entire game plays on a gamepad, mouse optional.
Playable on Steam Deck.
Supports Remote Play Together.
Runs offline.

store_data.about_the_game:
Summer 1992.... The country is about to change. Your club is in your hands.

A new league. New television money. Grounds that still smell of the old century, and a transfer market that still runs on handshakes, phone calls and nerve.

You are the manager. Not a passenger in a highlight reel — the person who picks the side, spends the money, fills the ground and lives with the board.

Retro Club Dynasty is a management journey through the first decade of the new top flight era: 1992/93 to 2001/02. Start small or start hungry. By the end of the decade the game you inherited will not be the game you are playing.

This is not a frozen 1992 toy. The world evolves with the seasons.

Key features

  • Era transfer & scouting

The market still has an old-school pulse. Windows close. Agents hover. You can tap up a target before the deal is public and poach academy kids before anyone else has clocked them. Scout properly, move quietly, and live with the fallout if you get caught wanting someone else's player.

  • Era evolution — watch the money explode

Year one is tight. Then the boom hits. Transfer fees swell. Wage bills swell. One bad contract can haunt you for seasons. The clubs that spend bravely can buy the decade. The clubs that panic get eaten. Bigger money. Bigger wages. Bigger risks. Your call.

  • Era tactics that grow with the years

Put players anywhere on the pitch. Draw the shape you actually want, not a pre-set from a booklet. As the seasons roll, the way football is played changes with you — more width, more pressing, more invention — if you have the personnel and the bottle to go with it.

  • Era sponsorship that builds the club

Shirt deals are not wallpaper. Land the right partner and the coffers move. Miss the wave and you watch rival clubs print money while you still argue over a local firm on the chest. Profile, cash, and status all travel together.

  • Era stadiums — bums on seats, money every week

A ground is a weekly machine. Fill it and the cash pumps in. Redevelop, chase capacity, and treat matchday like the business it is becoming. Empty seats in a boom decade are a confession.

A decade, not a screenshot....

League, cups, Europe. A pyramid underneath you. A calendar that actually behaves like the era: long windows, a hard spring deadline, summers that rewrite the squad.

Mid-decade the old transfer shackles start to come off. Contracts mean different things. Foreign quotas shift. The clever clubs adapt. The stubborn ones get left with a wage bill and a story.

You don't inherit a finished giant. You make one

Pick a club. Set a starting XI. Cut a deal. Fill a stand. Ride the money — or get buried by it.

The decade is open. The board wants a dynasty. Success is up to you.

store_data.about_the_game:
Every machine in the city is on the same network, and the network stopped liking people about an hour ago. Cars drive themselves at you now. The third rail switches on whenever it wants. You're on foot with one weak gun.

SCRAPSTORM is a bullet-heaven roguelite for one to four players. A run takes 20-30 minutes. You'll lose most of the early ones, and then you'll find a card combination that shouldn't work, and you'll spend the next twenty minutes watching a whole district come apart.

100+ cards, and a lot of them are a bad idea

You level up constantly and every level offers you cards. The plain ones do what they say. The interesting ones charge you for it — extra projectiles that each hit softer, lifesteal that permanently eats your max HP, a fire rate boost that ruins your accuracy.

Taking the bad idea is usually how the good runs start.

Every district is participating

  • Streets — the traffic is possessed. It runs the junctions on a signal you can't see and it does not brake.

  • Subway — the third rails go live on a rhythm you can learn. The trains don't care that you learned it. Then the lights go out.

  • Rooftops — gaps, crosswind, ziplines, and a long way down.

Each district has objectives you're free to ignore. Hold an uplink for sixty seconds while everything in the area comes to see what the noise is. Crack a supply vault and deal with what was guarding it. Walk a rescue pod to safety at its speed, which is not your speed.

Co-op, and nobody sits out

Local co-op and Remote Play Together both work from day one.

store_data.about_the_game:
GRAVEFEVER is a survivors-style action roguelike about a fight you can't win. Monsters come in waves, then floods. You level up, choose your upgrades, unlock your kit piece by piece, and carve a path through five arenas. Eventually, the swarm will take you. The timer at the top of the screen shows your score.

How a run goes

You start in a quiet village with only your basic attack. After ten levels, you gain your first real skill. By level 30, the map's guardian, a bear the size of a house, comes looking for you. Defeating it opens a portal to somewhere worse. A decent run can last over half an hour, but most don't get close.

Three hunters

  • Fighter: a bare-knuckle brawler. He punches in an arc, pushes the swarm back, and won't stay dead (his passive is called Death Rattle).
  • Gunslinger: every sixth shot is a lucky round. He settles arguments with a falling nuke.
  • Sorcerer: he slows and freezes everything nearby, hides behind a shattering barrier, and brings an ice age to the crowd.
Each hunter has a basic attack, a passive ability, three skills that unlock as you level up, and a final evolution at level 90.

Five arenas, four gatekeepers

The world changes every 30 levels; you'll move from the village to a glowing forest, a desert war camp, a mushroom glade, and a graveyard. You can only advance after defeating the mega-boss guarding the way out. Each one has its own fighting style: a triple rampage charge, a vanish-and-ambush teleport, skullfire mortars, and lingering spore pools. If you dodge their big attacks, they stagger and take double damage. If you face-tank them, well...

Builds that actually branch

Every level-up presents three cards. Core stats stack ten deep, and each skill has two upgrade branches leading to a capstone—choose one of two, and it's permanent. Specialist stats, like Bloodlust and Momentum, become available in the late game. A complete build can turn the endgame into a harvest. The combo counter has no cap; some players have surpassed 5,000.

The grave pays out

Death ends the run, not your progress. A complete death report shows what killed you and what damage you dealt. Gold is banked into the Armory for permanent stat training and a once-per-run second life. Quests reward you for your records. Once you've fought your way to a certain level, Head Start allows future runs to begin at level 10, 30, 60, 90, or 120—skip the warm-up and start at the part that kills you.

Also in the box

  • Cursed shrines that triple the spawn rate for 45 seconds—survive it and get rewarded
  • Random kill events provide double and triple XP windows and damage surges
  • Watch out for exploding suiciders, spitting casters, and a critter stuffed with gold that runs from you
  • Map hazards, mega-boss treasure chests, and per-map pickup buffs
  • A death recap shows exactly whose fault it was (yours)
  • Keyboard-first controls come with optional mouse aim, two UI themes, and Steam Cloud saves

About This Game

Water Sort: Alchemy is a relaxing 3D liquid-sorting puzzle game set in a warm and mysterious alchemy workshop.

Pour colorful liquids between glass bottles, separate each color, and restore order to every flask. The rules are simple to understand, but each new puzzle requires careful planning as the number of bottles, colors, and obstacles increases.

Enjoy the satisfying motion of flowing liquids, polished glass visuals, and a calm puzzle experience designed to be played at your own pace.

Simple Rules, Satisfying Puzzles

Your goal is simple: sort the liquids until every bottle contains only one color.

You may pour liquid into another bottle when:

  • The destination bottle has enough space.

  • The top liquid color matches.

  • Or the destination bottle is empty.

A single wrong move can block your solution, so think ahead and find the correct pouring order.

A Relaxing Alchemy Workshop

Solve puzzles surrounded by glass bottles, colorful potions, warm lighting, and the atmosphere of a cozy alchemy laboratory.

Every pour is presented in full 3D, with smooth bottle movement and colorful layered liquids that make sorting satisfying to watch as well as solve.

Hundreds of Levels

Progress through a large collection of puzzles with gradually increasing difficulty.

Early levels are designed for relaxing play, while later puzzles require more planning, more colors, and increasingly complex bottle arrangements.

Whether you want to solve a few quick puzzles or spend a long session mastering difficult stages, there is always another flask waiting to be sorted.

Play at Your Own Pace

There are no advertisements, energy systems, forced purchases, or mobile-style interruptions.

Buy the game once and enjoy the complete puzzle experience whenever you want.

Use undo and restart options whenever you need them, experiment with different solutions, and take as much time as you like.

Features

  • Relaxing water-sorting puzzle gameplay

  • Fully 3D glass bottles and colorful liquids

  • Smooth and satisfying pouring animations

  • Hundreds of progressively challenging levels

  • Simple controls and easy-to-understand rules

  • Undo and restart functions

  • A warm alchemy-inspired visual style

  • No advertisements

  • No energy system

  • No microtransactions

  • A complete premium puzzle experience

Sort every color, fill every flask, and become a master of liquid alchemy.

store_data.about_the_game:
Larina is a single-player turn-based fantasy RPG built around character progression, dungeon exploration, and an enormous variety of loot.

Build your hero through different combat Souls, develop their skills and attributes, hunt for powerful equipment, and explore a world filled with dungeons, quests, dangerous bosses, and repeatable endgame challenges.

Build Your Hero

Change the way you fight by acquiring and developing different Souls, each with its own skills, weapons, mechanics, and play-style. Build around Strength, Dexterity, Intellect and Stamina. Hire a mercenary companion, and experiment with combinations of equipment and abilities to shape how your character fights!

Hunt for Better Gear

Defeat enemies and bosses to find a crazy variety of equipment. Items have a number of different rarities and affixes that can be found on them. Items can be crafted using materials, or modified using magical orbs.

Dungeon bosses have their own special equipment sets, giving you a reason to return for another run, while crafting systems let you modify, re-roll, enchant and synthesise equipment as your character grows.

(An example of a typical "Rare" rarity item. The blue text is the implicit stats of that particular item. This means that every "Gilded Ring" base item type will have some Strength and some Maximum Health increase.)

Explore Larina

Travel between towns, forests, temples, castles, caves, and other dangerous locations across the world. Dungeons contain battles, treasures, puzzles, environmental hazards, and bosses, with new areas becoming accessible as your hero grows stronger.

Towns provide places to rest, shop, store equipment, recruit mercenaries, accept quests, and make use of specialised crafting services.

Maps and Endgame Challenges

In your journey, Maps open the door to repeatable adventures with randomised layouts, enemies, events, and modifiers. Just like equipment, Maps also have a variety of affixes that can modify how the adventure will go. The more dangerous the modifiers, the more rewarding the loot becomes!

Hunt for special Unique Maps that completely change the rules, enter the Arena for escalating combat trials, or slay dungeon bosses to complete their dedicated equipment sets.

Core Mechanics/Lore

Larina is built from years of ideas gathered from the RPGs, dungeon crawlers and loot-driven games I grew up playing, combining turn-based combat with deep itemisation, character building, dungeon exploration, and repeatable endgame systems.

Larina also returns to the setting of my original 2019 game (Candera: the Forgotten Realm), re-imagining that world with a much larger focus on exploration, character progression and loot!

Features:

  • Turn-based side-view combat

  • Multiple playable combat Souls (classes) with distinct skills and mechanics

  • Extensive Normal, Magic, Rare, Set, and Unique itemisation

  • Hundreds of equipment bases with inherent modifiers

  • Item crafting, enchanting, and synthesis

  • Mercenary companions to recruit

  • Dungeons, quests, bosses and puzzles

  • Repeatable Maps with randomised layouts and modifiers

  • Special Unique Maps with altered rules and rewards

  • Arena challenges and long-term character progression

  • Large inter-connected fantasy world to explore
