Powdertron is a physics playground where the chemistry is real. Its 674 materials — pure elements, compounds, alloys, minerals and industrial stock — each carry a genuine density, melting point, boiling point and formula, and 1,409 reaction rules decide what happens when they meet. Iron rusts. Sodium explodes in water. Limestone calcines. Nothing here is a lookup table of pretty colors.

Chemistry

Paint sand, water, acid, thermite or plasma onto a canvas of up to 120,000 cells and let it run. Heat it, freeze it, set it alight, pull the air out to a vacuum or switch gravity off entirely. Phase changes, combustion, dissolution, radioactive decay, heat conduction and structural collapse all play out cell by cell in a multithreaded C++ engine — fast enough that a full canvas still runs smoothly.

Electronics

A real circuit simulator, not a wiring puzzle. Batteries, resistors, capacitors, inductors, logic gates, seven-segment displays and an oscilloscope, connected by actual nets rather than cell adjacency. Build something that works, package it into a named chip, and drop that chip into your next design.

Wind Tunnel

Draw a shape, put it in the airflow, and see what happens. A lattice-Boltzmann solver renders live streamlines, pressure across the surface of the body, and the point where the flow separates.

Optics Bench

Lenses, mirrors and prisms with wavelength-accurate refraction. Split white light into its spectrum, chase a focal point, or build something that shouldn't work and find out why it doesn't.

Learn it by breaking it

Every material carries its real formula and properties, and reactions you trigger are logged as discoveries as you find them. A guided tutorial and a set of story challenges give you somewhere to start if a blank canvas is too much choice.

Build together

Host a session over Steam and share a canvas with friends. Everyone paints into the same world, sees each other's cursors, and watches the same simulation run. Name your worlds, give each its own physics settings, and lock the session with a password if you'd rather keep it private.

Make it yours

Add your own materials through the mods folder, save and load worlds, capture screenshots, and export measurement data straight to CSV for when the sandbox turns into an experiment.

store_data.about_the_game:
In CLI: Colony Line Interface, you will attempt to manage a space station using nothing but a command line.

Below you lies a dead Earth. Nothing remains, only signals waiting to be heard. Your station is humanity's last outpost capable of survival. Will you find other survivors? Or the resources needed to keep going?

Streams of data await analysis: every system, every colonist, every breath of the station passes through your terminal. No one will act for you. You delegate, interpret, decide.

Key Features:

  • The Crew: Assign tasks to colonists and leverage their aptitudes. They learn and improve, but they also age; their time is limited, and their skills die with them. Each colonist possesses unique traits, which can be a powerful asset or a dangerous drawback.

  • Life Support Systems: The station's module system is a living, interconnected machine. Electrolysis splits water to produce oxygen, but water is precious and finite. You need it for drinking and for the greenhouse, and the recycling system can't recover it all. CO₂ is the silent poison: filters trap it, but they saturate over time and must be maintained before the air becomes unbreathable. Every choice made on one system directly impacts another.

  • Production: Cultivate the greenhouse to harvest crops and convert them into rations, or synthesize the proteins needed to keep your colonists in good physical condition. The workshop is vital for crafting the materials required for maintenance and for expanding the station with new modules.

  • Signals & Missions: Outfit a shuttle and send a crew down to the planet, following signals intercepted onboard the station. Will you retrieve precious water for your reserves, or rescue surviving colonists?

  • Power: A central power generator fuels the station, its modules, and its machinery. Total power output is limited, choose carefully where to allocate it.

  • Integrity & Operating Regimes: Monitor the wear and tear of every system. Machines and modules degrade over time. You can push a module beyond its normal operating regime, but wear will accelerate significantly.

store_data.about_the_game:
You are a monkey... with a gun. Its your destiny to escape the zoo and find the legendary banana in the sky (The moon)

Shoot the floor and fly like a monkey can!
Every jump is a rocket-jump. Aim at the ground, fire, and launch yourself — TF2-style — across gaps, up ledges, and off walls. Master the recoil and wobble. Miss one angle and… well... 

The wobble
Your are a monkey, you dont know how to operate a gun... Its floppy, awkward and gloriously hard to control. Every shot sends you tumbling, spinning, and overcorrecting into disaster. It's not a bug — it's the whole game. Too much? Flip on Easy Mode for stable, no-wobble aiming and climb in peace. Leave it off for maximum chaos

One bad shot drops you ALL the way down
There's no floor under your mistakes. The world spirals upward around an open drop, so a single mistimed blast can send you plummeting past minutes of progress — screaming the whole way. Brutal? Yes. Fair? …Mostly. Impossible to put down? Absolutely.

Built to be clipped
This is a game made for that one perfect fail. Ragdoll tumbles, ridiculous physics, and last-second saves turn every run into a highlight reel. Rage, Skill , laugh, rage again, and smash "just one more try."

Features

  • Rocket-jump platforming with a gun that only launches you as primary movement

  • A wobbly, physics-driven monkey that's a joy (and a nightmare) to control

  • Easy Mode: no wobble, more checkpoints, a chill climb

  • A tall, spiraling escape from the zoo to freedom, where every fall counts

  • Ragdoll chaos and pratfalls built for streaming and clips

  • Simple to learn, brutal to master, impossible to rage-quit for good

Help Odysseus navigate the nine islands of Homer's Odyssey to return home and break the curse of Poseidon.  Explore new islands, craft your way to new tools, survive the wilderness and nights and solve island challenges to return to the sea.

store_data.about_the_game:
Thrown into the Cursed Forest for your past crimes, you have nothing but a fire to see and a sword to defend against the vile creatures that lurk within its shadows. You must balance combating the monsters and maintaining your tools until the end of each progressively intense night, because even a single misstep spells your doom. 

Creatures of the Forest

Face up to four aggressive monsters, each with their own personality and attack patterns. They will show no mercy, they will not leave without force, and they will one-shot you if not careful.

The Lonesome Camp

As the fire fades, the darkness closes in. It is up to you to stoke the flames, sharpen your blade, and look towards the skies for whatever might be looking back. 

Custom Night

Beat Night 5 to enter the Custom Night, where you can scale the difficulty of each creature to your liking. Good luck in CHAOS mode though, because I can't even beat it.

Other Stuff!

Piece together the confusing lore written in my horrible handwriting, learn how to draw both the knight and creatures for your math notes, and unveil like four secrets throughout your stay in the Cursed Forest.

store_data.about_the_game:
Humanity survived the collapse of Earth—but it did not survive united.

Across the Broken Rift, rival descendants of the human diaspora struggle over isolated colonies, failing trade routes, and technology left behind by the mysterious Elders. As a frontier Captain of the Aurelian Directorate, restore your worlds, rebuild your fleets, and decide how far you will go to stop the Veyran Dominion from ruling what remains.

Broken Rift: Dominion is a real-time 4X strategy game connecting empire management, fleet movement, tactical space combat, colony construction, espionage, diplomacy, and ground warfare inside one continuous campaign.

Face Empires That Think—and Remember

A fully offline, locally embedded LLM helps drive every major rival faction. This is not a cloud chatbot attached to a traditional opponent: factions use their own personalities, ambitions, intelligence, and save-persistent history to make connected decisions across the campaign.

  • Pursue an agenda: expand, prepare invasions, reinforce endangered worlds, recover from defeat, or consolidate for the next war.

  • Build an empire: balance power, housing, food, security, laboratories, production, fortifications, and a treasury that cannot fund everything at once.

  • Research a technological future: prioritize weapons, shields, propulsion, sensors, industry, or espionage using real monthly research income.

  • Negotiate in character: pursue trade, pacts, alliances, peace, tribute, threats, insults, and war according to personality, relations, and military strength.

  • Fight in the shadows: conduct reconnaissance, steal research, sabotage assets, disrupt fleets, and defend against hostile agents.

  • Remember the consequences: victories, humiliations, losses, treaties, discoveries, and abandoned plans influence later choices.

The complete model ships inside the game. There is no separate download, cloud inference service, subscription, API key, account requirement, or campaign data sent to an external server. Deterministic simulation rules remain authoritative over costs, legal actions, targeting, combat, and outcomes. If compatible GPU acceleration is unavailable—or if you prefer to disable Smart AI—authored strategic logic takes command so the war can continue.

Command Every Layer of the War

Rule a living frontier

Develop colonies whose populations need power, food, housing, security, and functioning infrastructure. Set tax policy, manage morale, expand research, automate construction priorities, and respond as growing worlds demand more from their cities.

Every colony is a real planetary surface. Place buildings on its top-down grid, expand production, position defensive tanks around the Nexus, and prepare the same terrain for a future invasion.

Move real fleets through real space

Fleets travel across the galaxy instead of teleporting between planets. Order them into deep space, pursue radar contacts, merge task forces, split fleets, transfer tanks near friendly worlds, or intercept an enemy before it reaches a vulnerable colony.

Radar matters. Undiscovered worlds remain unknown, hostile fleets can disappear beyond sensor range, and an unpowered planetary radar leaves a genuine hole in your intelligence network.

Shape battle before the first shot

Space battles begin paused. Arrange ships into Line, Wedge, or Screen formations, place individual vessels inside your deployment zone, assign targets, protect transports, and set fighter posture before pressing Start.

Once combat begins, issue movement and attack orders, pause to reassess, focus fire, or retreat before a bad engagement becomes a destroyed fleet. Fighters harass enemy formations or screen allied capital ships, while transports carry the armor needed to conquer worlds.

Fight for the surface

Winning orbit is only the beginning. A fleet needs tank capacity and embarked ground armor to take a defended colony. Deploy attackers along the outskirts, reposition established defenders, lay specialized mines, and command combined armored forces through a top-down ground assault.

Design the Forces You Need

Configure future production for frigates, destroyers, corvettes, cruisers, transports, orbital stations, fighters, tanks, and dreadnoughts. Combine distinct primary and secondary weapons, six shield tiers, radar arrays, engines, torpedoes, cargo bays, ECM, defensive pods, mine pods, regeneration, and other specialized modules.

Newly commissioned units inherit the design that existed when production began. Better equipment raises the price, so the strongest blueprint is not always the fleet your economy can afford.

The Elder Legacy Campaign

Restore Aurelia's shattered frontier, defend a Trade Federation envoy, assault a Dominion stronghold, conduct covert reconnaissance, and survive the retaliation that follows.

Beyond the frontier lie five Elder caches containing components of a warship beyond anything the modern factions can build. Each operation has a deadline. Reach a cache first and claim its advantage; fail, and the story routes into a harder recovery operation instead of simply ending the campaign.

Between major operations, shorter frontier events feed credits, research, and pressure into the strategic war. Assemble the Elder Warship and the galaxy will see the Directorate as an overwhelming force. Lose it to the Dominion and decide whether humanity's last resistance will surrender—or fight a war it may no longer be able to win.

Skirmish Mode

Create a custom conflict across 20, 50, or 100 planets. Choose your faction, starting treasury, technology level, and participating AI powers. Rival empires research, develop colonies, build fleets and armor, negotiate treaties, form alliances, and pursue a shared victory condition: become the last power standing—or survive as part of the final alliance.

Key Features

  • Continuous strategic play spanning galaxy, colony, space, and ground layers

  • Physical fleets with travel time, radar visibility, pursuit, merging, splitting, and tank transport

  • Paused pre-battle planning with formations, targets, fighter postures, and transport protection

  • Top-down colony construction and ground warfare on the same planetary surfaces

  • Detailed ship, fighter, tank, and station designs with equipment-based pricing

  • Per-planet production queues and population-driven taxes, research, morale, growth, and trade

  • Persistent spies with missions, attributes, experience, levels, and counterintelligence

  • Diplomacy shaped by relations, treaties, strength, personalities, and recent history

  • Fully offline Smart AI with persistent faction plans, intelligence, research, and strategic memory

  • Deterministic and authored fallbacks that preserve legal game outcomes

  • A voiced story campaign with branching recovery operations and persistent endgame choices

  • Custom skirmishes across galaxies of up to 100 planets

  • Remember the consequences: victories, humiliations, losses, treaties, discoveries, and abandoned plans influence later choices.

The complete model ships inside the game. There is no separate download, cloud inference service, subscription, API key, account requirement, or campaign data sent to an external server. Deterministic simulation rules remain authoritative over costs, legal actions, targeting, combat, and outcomes. If compatible GPU acceleration is unavailable—or if you prefer to disable Smart AI—authored strategic logic takes command so the war can continue.

Command Every Layer of the War

Rule a living frontier

Develop colonies whose populations need power, food, housing, security, and functioning infrastructure. Set tax policy, manage morale, expand research, automate construction priorities, and respond as growing worlds demand more from their cities.

Every colony is a real planetary surface. Place buildings on its top-down grid, expand production, position defensive tanks around the Nexus, and prepare the same terrain for a future invasion.

Move real fleets through real space

Fleets travel across the galaxy instead of teleporting between planets. Order them into deep space, pursue radar contacts, merge task forces, split fleets, transfer tanks near friendly worlds, or intercept an enemy before it reaches a vulnerable colony.

Radar matters. Undiscovered worlds remain unknown, hostile fleets can disappear beyond sensor range, and an unpowered planetary radar leaves a genuine hole in your intelligence network.

Shape battle before the first shot

Space battles begin paused. Arrange ships into Line, Wedge, or Screen formations, place individual vessels inside your deployment zone, assign targets, protect transports, and set fighter posture before pressing Start.

Once combat begins, issue movement and attack orders, pause to reassess, focus fire, or retreat before a bad engagement becomes a destroyed fleet. Fighters harass enemy formations or screen allied capital ships, while transports carry the armor needed to conquer worlds.

Fight for the surface

Winning orbit is only the beginning. A fleet needs tank capacity and embarked ground armor to take a defended colony. Deploy attackers along the outskirts, reposition established defenders, lay specialized mines, and command combined armored forces through a top-down ground assault.

Design the Forces You Need

Configure future production for frigates, destroyers, corvettes, cruisers, transports, orbital stations, fighters, tanks, and dreadnoughts. Combine distinct primary and secondary weapons, six shield tiers, radar arrays, engines, torpedoes, cargo bays, ECM, defensive pods, mine pods, regeneration, and other specialized modules.

Newly commissioned units inherit the design that existed when production began. Better equipment raises the price, so the strongest blueprint is not always the fleet your economy can afford.

The Elder Legacy Campaign

Restore Aurelia's shattered frontier, defend a Trade Federation envoy, assault a Dominion stronghold, conduct covert reconnaissance, and survive the retaliation that follows.

Beyond the frontier lie five Elder caches containing components of a warship beyond anything the modern factions can build. Each operation has a deadline. Reach a cache first and claim its advantage; fail, and the story routes into a harder recovery operation instead of simply ending the campaign.

Between major operations, shorter frontier events feed credits, research, and pressure into the strategic war. Assemble the Elder Warship and the galaxy will see the Directorate as an overwhelming force. Lose it to the Dominion and decide whether humanity's last resistance will surrender—or fight a war it may no longer be able to win.

Skirmish Mode

Create a custom conflict across 20, 50, or 100 planets. Choose your faction, starting treasury, technology level, and participating AI powers. Rival empires research, develop colonies, build fleets and armor, negotiate treaties, form alliances, and pursue a shared victory condition: become the last power standing—or survive as part of the final alliance.

Key Features

  • Continuous strategic play spanning galaxy, colony, space, and ground layers

  • Physical fleets with travel time, radar visibility, pursuit, merging, splitting, and tank transport

  • Paused pre-battle planning with formations, targets, fighter postures, and transport protection

  • Top-down colony construction and ground warfare on the same planetary surfaces

  • Detailed ship, fighter, tank, and station designs with equipment-based pricing

  • Per-planet production queues and population-driven taxes, research, morale, growth, and trade

  • Persistent spies with missions, attributes, experience, levels, and counterintelligence

  • Diplomacy shaped by relations, treaties, strength, personalities, and recent history

  • Fully offline Smart AI with persistent faction plans, intelligence, research, and strategic memory

  • Deterministic and authored fallbacks that preserve legal game outcomes

  • A voiced story campaign with branching recovery operations and persistent endgame choices

  • Custom skirmishes across galaxies of up to 100 planets

store_data.about_the_game:
"We hope you're enjoying the arcade! Huh, you want to leave? No no, you don't want to leave...not for a...long time..."

They Keep Rolling is an incremental ball-roller about earning trillions of tokens. Roll. Upgrade. Hire. Repeat. Before long, this whole cozy-creepy arcade is blinking and the prize counter is empty.

Roll, score, repeat
Line up your throw and let it fly. Land the high rings for big payouts, upgrade the ball for point increases, and pour everything you earn straight back into the machines.

Put the arcade on autopilot
Hire other animals in the arcade to roll for you. Buy pizza and sodas for the crew. Upgrade their machines too to go from millions to kabillions of tokens.

Every machine has a trick
No two machines play the same. Leaf tornadoes that hurl your ball upwards. Ghosts that grant extra tokens. The deeper you go, the stranger the machines get.

Meet the regulars
A twitchy grey squirrel who loves the games a little too much. A aimless deer looking for a break. A quiet raccoon who seems to know something you don't. The animals of Whispering Pines Arcade each have a story, and the longer you stay, the more you wonder...why do none of them ever leave?

Wrapped in a chunky PSX art style, warm 2000's arcade aesthetic, and the quiet hum of Appalachia, They Keep Rolling is easy to start and hard to put down.

Features

  • Ball-rolling built on an incremental economy that compounds every run

  • Dozens of upgrades that grow a single machine into a whole arcade floor

  • Hire friends to earn idle earnings, so your tokens keep climbing while you strategize

  • A cast of Appalachian animal regulars with a slow-burning mystery underneath

  • Prestige runs with permanent upgrades and more than one way to build

store_data.about_the_game:
The world outside doesn't exist anymore — or it never did. All that remains is the Store, an endless structure holding back the nothing beyond its walls. You run it. You're the only one who remembers why.

Each day, the Store opens its doors to more customers than the last — humanoid figures who are never quite human, drawn in by hunger, curiosity, or something else entirely. Some browse. Some buy. Many steal. Your job is to keep the shelves full, the registers running, and the losses low for as long as you possibly can — because there is no winning, only surviving.

Gameplay

Manage a live, escalating retail simulation where the customer count and theft rate climb with every day survived. Place and arrange furniture and shelving with full collision-aware layout tools across multiple buildings and stacked floors. Hire and assign a staff of Generalists, Stockers, Cashiers, Security, and Janitors, each with individual stats for speed, stock handling, range, patience, and salary. Operate through a full day/night cycle — customers flood in from open to close while your crew clocks out at night, leaving the store to reset before the next wave.

Progression & Systems

Build out your store and workforce to keep pace with an economy that never stops escalating. Balance staffing costs against theft losses as the difficulty curve steepens day over day. Refine your store layout and worker assignments to survive longer runs, with each attempt shaped by the choices made in the one before it.

Features

  • Roguelike escalation — no two runs end the same way

  • Deep staffing system with 5 distinct worker roles and individual stats

  • Full store-building sim with collision-aware furniture placement across multiple floors

  • Dynamic day/night cycle driving customer spawns and worker shifts

  • Anti-theft gameplay loop — station Security and catch shoplifters before they clean you out

  • Unsettling, unexplained setting populated by humanoid customers and workers who are never quite human

Current Content

  • Core store-building, staffing, and checkout systems implemented

  • Day/night cycle and theft escalation fully functional

  • Save/load system in place

store_data.about_the_game:
A young man has struggled his entire life with finding a girlfriend. He lives in a small town known as Rook's Landing and has never had a relationship. That is... until he discovered a new trending app called Girlfriend GPT. 

This new app pledges to help him find a girlfriend. Despite having doubts, he decides to play along and see what happens.

Will Girlfriend GPT's advice be enough to secure him his very first girlfriend? Only time will tell.

Follow the advice of Girlfriend GPT and chase a pretty girl around town and try to find out more about her in this short mini-story.  You'll experience romance, comedy, and humor throughout your adventure.

Featuring high quality cinematic scenes throughout your journey, while also allowing you to explore several parts of Rook's Landing city. There are multiple destinations to visit as you try to achieve your quest in finding a girlfriend.

Along the way you'll be able to review your city map and follow the quest set forth by Girlfriend GPT.  

FEATURES:

  • HDRP Cinematic Scenes

  • Open World Adventure

  • Multiple Destinations

  • Voice Acting

  • Steam Achievements

store_data.about_the_game:
Autolantis blends city-building with roguelite strategy. Place Tiles, assign Workers, and enact Policies to create an automated production engine that grows exponentially. Build a one-of-a-kind empire on a uniquely generated land each run, and watch your civilization climb to its peak.

Countless Building Strategies

  • Place Tiles of different shapes and sizes, each with its own strengths, and position them for maximum effect

  • Assign Workers with unique Effects to grant Tiles powerful permanent Bonuses

  • Enact powerful Policies suited to your build and push Tile synergies beyond their limits

  • Piece together Territories with different shapes and terrain to create a one-of-a-kind map

  • Gain Authority in a variety of ways, then spend it during Council to strengthen your build

Eureka!

  • Three matching Tiles automatically merge and upgrade, triggering Eureka! and giving you access to powerful Tiles unavailable through regular choices

Hands-Off, Explosive Production

  • After making your decisions each Year, sit back and watch your empire coordinate production automatically through all four Seasons

  • Clear, satisfying animations let you follow every synergy as it unfolds

  • Speed controls and automatic Resource collection keep the action moving

  • Exponential growth turns your production engine into an endless cascade of Resources

A Fresh Challenge Every Run

  • Territory choices are randomized every run, changing how you piece together the map

  • Natural Tiles are randomized every run; use careful planning to turn obstacles into opportunities

  • Events are randomized every run, challenging you to make the decisions that maximize their rewards

  • Keep your empire running with a limited number of decisions, then push for even greater rewards

More Content and Features

  • 4 playable Leaders, each with an entirely different pool of build options

  • 250+ Tiles with distinct Effects

  • 150+ Policies that can reshape the course of a run

  • 100+ Workers with unique Effects

  • 50+ Eureka Tiles that push your build beyond its limits

  • 30+ unexpected dynamic Events

  • 10 Difficulty levels to conquer

  • A satisfying automated production cycle spanning all four Seasons

  • Compete with other players for the highest rank

Everything Hates Me is a peaceful 2D platformer where absolutely nothing wants to hurt you.

  • The floor is trustworthy.
    The signs never lie.
    The trees are friendly.
    The exit definitely won't run away.

Probably.

Your only job is simple:

Reach the exit.

Unfortunately, the game has other plans.

  • Hundreds of traps, tricks, and terrible ideas

  • Floors that stop being floors

  • Walls that may need to be ridden

  • Signs containing highly questionable advice

  • Objects that are sometimes enemies and sometimes the solution

  • Fast deaths and even faster retries

  • Old traps returning exactly when you forgot about them

  • A developer who is definitely on your side

THE RULES ARE SIMPLE:

Die.

Learn what killed you.

Die again.

Realize you learned the wrong lesson.

Eventually reach the exit.

Maybe.

EVERYTHING HATES YOU.

The floor hates you.
The walls hate you.
The trees hate you.
The game hates you.

And by the end...

you might hate the developer too.

store_data.about_the_game:
You are the producer.

Signing a trainee is just the beginning. After that you need lyricists, composers, and choreographers. You need to build a company that can actually produce music from scratch. And when you finally get that first single out the door, there are eleven other labels already on the chart waiting for you.

But the hardest part isn't running the company. It's the people.

Every trainee has a path they want to take, a temper you'll learn about, and one thing they'll never budge on. She asked for a week off — you filled her schedule with appearances. She said she wanted to help write — you went with someone else's lyrics at the greenlight. She remembers all of it, and the next time you open a conversation, you'll know.

You can put her on variety shows and music competitions, a dozen-plus episodes at a stretch. Good results build a reputation; the right positioning makes it stick. You can also treat her as a pure business investment — but she won't treat you as just a boss. Relationships can turn romantic. Romance won't make her easier to manage, won't put extra money in your pocket. It only changes the way she talks to you, and what you'll have to deal with next.

Features


• Build an entertainment company from scratch — hire staff, develop departments, create lyrics, compositions, and choreography with your own team
• Compete head-to-head against eleven rival labels across six regional charts, with weekly rankings and year-end awards
• Send trainees to variety shows, music competitions, and acting competitions — a dozen-plus episodes per season, with on-set crises that fall on your shoulders
• Trainees remember every promise you make — delivery is measured by the schedule you set, not the words you said
• Relationships can develop into romance — attraction, jealousy, and real feelings happen, but romance offers no management advantage
• Create your own trainees through the Steam Workshop, or use ones other players have built

Online

Trainee dialogue is generated by an online AI service. Internet connection required throughout play. Management, releases, and settlement all run locally.

The game interface is available in Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your job is to explore an office swallowed by darkness, photograph traces left behind by spirits, and report them.

Almost all of the lights are gone, making it difficult to see your surroundings with the naked eye.

The only thing you can rely on is the camera in your hands.

Photograph the traces—and escape the phenomena.

Explore the Darkness Through Your Camera

Fire the flash to briefly reveal your surroundings in the darkness.

The camera also has night vision, allowing you to see things in the dark that are invisible to the naked eye.

Search the office using both flash and night vision, and look for "traces" that are clearly out of place.

Photograph and Report the Traces

When you find something suspicious, take a photo that captures it.

You can review your photos on the camera. Select and tag the photos containing traces, then submit your report from a terminal in the office.

Report the correct trace and the elevator will activate, allowing you to move on.

Repeat the process until the investigation is complete.

Even Pressing the Shutter Is Dangerous

You cannot simply photograph everything indiscriminately.

If you take a photo with no trace in it, something that was never really there may occasionally appear in the image.

The more spirit photographs you accumulate, the more likely dangerous paranormal phenomena are to occur in the office.

Before you press the shutter, decide whether there really is a trace there—and whether you should light the area first.

Traces and Paranormal Phenomena

What you are looking for are traces showing that a spirit was once there.

But during your investigation, paranormal phenomena may sometimes occur—signs that a spirit is "here, right now."

  • Sounds that should not be there.

  • Rooms that suddenly change.

  • Something appearing through the camera.

  • A presence behind you.

Each paranormal phenomenon has its own way to deal with it.

When something abnormal happens, look around carefully, listen, and decide what you need to do.

If you respond incorrectly, your investigation ends there.

Features

  • A short first-person psychological horror experience

  • Anomaly-hunting exploration in a pitch-dark office

  • A camera equipped with flash and night vision

  • A gameplay loop built around photographing anomalies, sorting photos, and reporting your findings

  • A spirit-photo system where careless shooting itself creates danger

  • A variety of paranormal phenomena that occur at random

  • Exploration where you must identify each phenomenon and respond correctly to survive

store_data.about_the_game:
Altstadt is a relaxing building toy about shaping a colorful miniature German old town. Place houses and streets on a compact board and watch a small settlement grow into a detailed diorama. There are no resources, budgets, or populations to manage. Just build, experiment, and refine.

BUILD HOUSE BY HOUSE

Start with individual houses. Make them taller or lower them again, or expand them into larger connected buildings. Lay streets to form paved squares and intimate courtyards. Entrances, shared walls, and rooflines adapt to the town you build, and eligible lanes can even become covered Schwibbogen passages.

MAKE IT YOURS

Choose coordinated facade and roof colors for each complete building. Renovate a house to try another compatible architectural design without rebuilding the layout you like. Undo and redo let you experiment freely until every corner feels right.

BUILD WITHOUT PRESSURE

There is no money, score, timer, objective, or failure state. Chimney smoke, shutters, laundry, greenery, and small movements give your finished streets an inhabited feeling without turning the town into a management simulation. Keep refining one composition or clear the board and begin again.

store_data.about_the_game:
Meeting a Most Unusual Cat
In the wake of a disaster, a mysterious cat who can change its form saves you. You name it “Mio” after the sound it makes. You and Mio now share the same heartbeat—but that doesn't mean you're always on the same page. After all, it's a cat. It has its own habits, its own moods, and a whole trail of questions: Where did it come from? Why did it save you? How do you even get along with it? As you travel together, the answers begin to surface. But the real bond between you? That was never there from the start.

A Mother's Riddle
What are the silent giants? What is the newborn giant? Why are the Sentinels hunting your cat? And what, exactly, is your cat? Every thread leads back to your missing mother. To find her—and to find the truth—you follow the path she once walked. And the answer you'll uncover will go far beyond the questions you asked.

Knowledge-Driven Combat and Exploration This world feels familiar and strange all at once. The things you've always taken for granted—the shifting orbit of the Giant, the pulse of Ylem, the movements of the Sentinels—might hold rules you've never noticed. Learn how this world works. Observe what lies beneath the surface. That knowledge will keep you from losing your way, and it might just keep you alive in a fight. Knowledge is the strongest weapon you and Mio carry.

Perfect Sync……Maybe?
When you hit a wall or run into danger, don't forget your cat. There are problems only Mio can solve—sometimes gracefully, sometimes......less so. In combat, the more you learn to fight together, the easier it becomes. In exploration, keep an eye on Mio—the little cat has its own curiosities, and those might matter more than you think. Don't leave it behind. At the end of this road, you'll face something that only the two of you can complete together.

store_data.about_the_game:
So, you're the new night-shift station master. Listen carefully, because I won't be explaining this twice.

Your Duties

The first things you do are: check the timetable, route trains, sell tickets, make announcements, resolve any queries passengers might have, inspect the platforms, and ensure everything is in order.

Don't worry, very few trains pass through here at night.

A Few Things You Should Know

Now, there are some things that you'd learn when you've been working here for some time.

If you hear someone calling and laughing, don't go looking. There is nobody there.

If a passenger behaves strangely, handle it. Don't ask unnecessary questions.

And if you see something you can't explain...

...ignore it.

Most things around here are best left alone.

About the Train

Around 2:30 in the night, you will see a train arrive that isn't on the timetable.

Don't worry about it.

Don't signal it in. Don't try to contact the driver. Don't ask the passengers where they're going.

It arrives. It stops, and eventually... it leaves.

You keep doing your job.

That's all you need to know.

Follow the procedures, keep the station running, and you might survive the night.

Now Get To Work,

Your shift starts soon.

store_data.about_the_game:
A terrarium in the corner

Taskbar Slime: Tucked-Away Terrarium is an idle game about quietly watching the slimes that live in a terrarium tucked into the corner of your desktop. They are sensitive creatures — touch one and it splits in two. The rest of the time, they just wobble at the edge of your vision.

Give them something, and they change

Stone, an oak leaf, water, a bird's feather. Take a material from the shelf and hand it to a slime, and the slime takes it in and becomes something else. The same stone turns a red one into this and a green one into that. The slimes drop materials themselves, a little at a time, so there is nothing to go out and farm.

It keeps growing while you are not looking

Left alone, slimes bump into one another and mix. They swell larger, or turn into something else entirely. New kinds arrive even when all you are doing is watching.

Everything you find goes in the codex

Every slime you find is recorded in your codex, and there are over 300 kinds in all. Watch at your own pace, hand out a material now and then, and work your way towards a complete collection.

store_data.about_the_game:
BLACKBEAM is a top-down sci-fi action adventure combining exploration, combat, crystal mining, and light base building.


Take control of a rover and traverse the surface of an alien planet. Discover new areas, smash crystal formations, battle hostile creatures, and venture ever farther in search of valuable resources and extraordinary finds.


By day, the world favors exploration and growth. After dark, visibility drops sharply, energy becomes more important, and the surface grows far more dangerous. You can return to the safety of your base facilities or stay out in the field and take a greater risk.


SET OUT ON EXPEDITIONS
Drive your rover across an alien world, discover new places, and venture ever farther from your base. Every expedition may lead to new deposits, dangerous areas, and valuable finds.


SMASH AND MINE CRYSTALS
Find formations of alien crystals and smash them to gather the resources you need to progress. Better equipment will let you reach increasingly valuable deposits and mine them more effectively.


BATTLE ALIEN WILDLIFE
You are not alone on the surface. Evade attacks, use your rover's weapons, and battle creatures encountered while exploring. After night falls, they become a far greater threat.


UPGRADE YOUR ROVER AND BASE FACILITIES
Improve your rover's capabilities to travel farther, extract resources more efficiently, and handle threats more effectively. Expand your base and build the facilities you need to prepare for future expeditions.


MAKE THE MOST OF THE DAY. RISK THE NIGHT.
Daylight makes exploration, mining, and preparation easier. After dark, limited visibility, greater energy demands, and hostile activity change the rhythm of play. Returning to base is safer, but pressing on may be worth the risk.


VENTURE EVER FARTHER
Gather resources, improve your equipment, and expand your expedition's capabilities. With every upgrade, you can venture farther into the unknown and face increasingly challenging regions of the planet.


PLAY SOLO OR ONLINE
Explore the planet alone or enter an online world where the presence of other players brings added unpredictability, competition, and new threats.

store_data.about_the_game:
In a nightmare realm where memory, trauma, and emotion manifest as a horrifying reality,
you are a new soul trapped inside. Find your way out before the nightmare consumes you.

If something is in the room with you, don't move.

You are strapped into an old wheelchair. You hold two things: a flashlight, and a small bell.
When you think you're not alone, find them, send them away before they get too close.

Find them, be quick... They move closer when you're not looking.
Listen. When you believe they're gone, move on. 

Escape the nightmares, each with its own place, challenges, horrors.
Every nightmare introduces something new.

Not everything hunting you can be survived the same way.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Features

  • One sitting. ~1-2h gameplay, built to be played in the dark with headphones.

  • Accessibility: reduce jumpscare mode, reduced camera motion, brightness, controller support.

store_data.about_the_game:
[Story Background]

In the face of relentless waves of aberrant creatures, the Earth Allied Defense Front has committed nearly all its combat forces—yet the frontlines continue to collapse. With the Global Urban Defense Grid still weeks away from full deployment, the only remaining option is to deploy the last intact Dragoon Unit.

Players will take command of this elite squad of maid mecha兵士 (maid-type combat androids) on the outskirts of the city. Supported by overwhelming rear-echelon firepower, you must construct makeshift defensive lines using the terrain to hold back the tide of mutated enemies—buying precious time for the urban defense grid to establish its initial protective capability.

[Gameplay Overview]

Maid Mech : Backpack TD is a strategy game that blends modular backpack management​ with grid-based path tower defense.

At the end of each wave, players acquire functional modules of various shapes. By strategically assembling and expanding these modules on a 14×7​ battlefield grid, you gradually build your own layered defense system. Once the formation is complete, the mecha units deployed on the grid will automatically engage enemies advancing along predetermined paths.

Set against a modern warfare backdrop infused with a distinctive maid-and-mecha aesthetic, the game's core unit roster covers a wide range of tactical roles—offering deep strategic planning while delivering satisfying real-time action for tower defense enthusiasts.

store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]You cannot move. You cannot speak. You can only choose.[/h2]

You are a stone wishing well in a small seaside town. People lean over your edge, toss a coin, and whisper what they want most. Granting is your only voice — and your water is not endless.

[h2]Every wish has a price[/h2]

Eight townspeople return to you, day after day, for eight days. The merchant asks for a horse; days later he buys the field that fed the girl who greets you every morning. The game never blames you. It only shows you what you did — in the same faces, in the same square, one day later.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[list]

[*] 119 handwritten events across 8 days — each one someone's wish, or its consequence

[*] 8 characters whose fates intertwine: what you give one, you quietly take from another

[*] 4 endings, decided by the kind of well you chose to be

[*] The town remembers: choices persist and come back as props, lines and faces

[*] Two buttons: grant or refuse. (And one more, to skip.)

[*] A living square from dawn to dusk — visitors arrive with the sun

[*] One run: 70–80 minutes. Seeing everything: about four runs.

[*] Full controller support · playable in 22 languages

[/list]

[h2]Who is the well when the water runs low?[/h2]

Some wishes feed your depths; some drain them. Hold everything back and be forgotten. Give everything away and watch the town devour itself. Four ends of the same rope — and none of them is called "right".

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome Aboard the Sightless Ship

The rules aboard are simple:

All thefts must take place after the clock strikes midnight and before dawn.

If no one sees you steal it, then you didn’t steal it.

Use every trick at your disposal—gadgets, potions, magic, hypnosis, and sleight of hand.

Most importantly—don’t fall asleep first.

Only Those Who Close Their Eyes Can Be Robbed

This is a party game built around one crucial question: who will close their eyes first?

Watch your friends’ drooping eyelids. Decide whether they’re truly asleep. The moment their eyes close, reach out and steal—then scramble back to safety before they wake up.

Every closed eye sets up a new laugh. Every outstretched hand could make hunter and prey switch places in an instant.

Bluff your friends, stir up chaos, and seize every opportunity!

Outsmart and Outreact Your Rivals to Become a Legendary Thief

A true master thief relies not on force, but on observation, judgment, dexterity, and nerve.

Wait for your rivals’ weakest moments. Choose the prize worth risking everything for. Then drag the treasure from their territory back into your own—with your own hands.

Step onto the Secret Stage of the Gaslight Era

The Paris Exposition has only just drawn to a close, and electricity, cinema, railways, and modern forensic techniques are transforming the world. The gaslights still burn, but fingerprinting will soon give every person an identity that cannot be escaped. International trade has brought forth treasures unlike anything seen before—and turned theft into a precise art built on ingenious devices, disguise, psychological manipulation, and intelligence.

The Sightless Ship brings together master thieves from around the world, experts in stolen goods, occultists, and wealthy patrons who prefer to remain anonymous.

This is the final age in which a master thief can still don a mask, assume a false name, and vanish from the world without a trace.

store_data.about_the_game:
All Pool Players Go to Hell is a physics-based combat roguelite where your pool balls are your weapons, your deck determines your options, and every shot can send a carefully laid plan completely off the rails.

Build your deck, line up your shots, and use real-time physics to smash your way through the horrors standing between you and whatever passes for an "exit" around here.

And you won't be making the journey alone.

Scratch Jack will be accompanying you through the depths of Hell. He'll offer advice, commentary and, more often than not, mockery. Just don't get too comfortable. He's far from the only strange character waiting for you down there.

BUILD YOUR ARSENAL

Discover different types of pool balls, each changing the way you approach combat. Build a deck around your favourites and combine them with upgrades that alter their damage, force, behaviour and abilities.

Experiment with different combinations and turn a simple game of pool into something considerably more dangerous.

EVERY SHOT IS PHYSICS-DRIVEN

Combat takes place in real time using physics.

Choose your ball. Pick your angle. Decide how much force to put behind the shot and deal with the consequences.

Ricochets, collisions, positioning and momentum all matter. A well-placed shot can tear through a room. A badly placed one might leave you wishing you could blame the cue.

FIND YOUR OWN WAY THROUGH HELL

Every run generates a new path through each map.

Choose where to travel, decide which encounters are worth the risk, collect new cards and upgrades, and shape your build as you descend deeper.

With multiple maps to survive in each run, reaching the end won't be a matter of following the same route twice.

FACE WHAT'S WAITING AT THE END

Each map culminates in its own bespoke boss encounter, designed to put your build and your ability to actually play pool to the test.

On your way to them, you'll need to defend yourself against waves of Hell Spawn. Each one has different movements patterns, abilities, weight and damage. You'll need to react accordingly if you want a chance  to meet who waits at the end. 

Survive, and your journey continues deeper into Hell.

CHANGE HOW EVERY RUN BEGINS

Unlock and choose between different starting decks and abilities, giving you new foundations to build around from the moment a run begins.

Combine that with randomized paths, different ball types and a wide range of upgrades, and each descent gives you another opportunity to discover something completely ridiculous that somehow works.

On your way to them, you'll need to defend yourself against waves of Hell Spawn. Each one has different movements patterns, abilities, weight and damage. You'll need to react accordingly if you want a chance  to meet who waits at the end. 

Survive, and your journey continues deeper into Hell.

CHANGE HOW EVERY RUN BEGINS

Unlock and choose between different starting decks and abilities, giving you new foundations to build around from the moment a run begins.

Combine that with randomized paths, different ball types and a wide range of upgrades, and each descent gives you another opportunity to discover something completely ridiculous that somehow works.
store_data.short_description: All Pool Players Go to Hell is a physics-based combat roguelite where your pool balls are your weapons, your deck determines your options, and every shot can send a carefully laid plan completely off the rails. Build your deck, line up your shots, and use real-time physics to survive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Sophie II: Paradox is the sequel to Sophie: The Girl From The Zone. To save humanity, your mind was sent back into the past to rewrite history. The plan could have been simple, but everything went wrong. You did not wake up in your own body, but in Max's, a man with a very questionable reputation. Around you, no one knows what is really happening. Unable to reveal your true identity without risking causing a paradox, you will have to manipulate the events of the past, find crucial allies, and prevent the extinction of humanity.

Can the past truly be changed?
Will you survive your own choices?
And what if something else is hiding behind all of this?

  • A deeply cinematic narrative:
    Created by a true cinema enthusiast, the game breaks away from the usual conventions to immerse you in a mature, dark, and psychological universe.

  • Choices with a butterfly effect:
    Your decisions have real short-term and long-term consequences on the story. A choice that seems insignificant at the beginning of the game can change a great deal...

⚠️ Content Warning
This story explores the darkest aspects of human nature. The game contains extreme violence, gore, and explicit sexual content. (Note: a filter allows you to disable pornographic content and enjoy the story in a "Soft" mode, limited to nudity.)

💡 Do I need to have played the first game?
It is strongly recommended that you play Sophie: The Girl From The Zone in order to catch all the nuances, small plot details, and fully understand the universe. However... I strongly believe it could also be fascinating to approach the story the other way around and start directly with SOPHIE II!

All erotic scenes can be avoided.

store_data.about_the_game:
You are one of several gods competing in the Divine Exchange, a ruthless market where mortal lives become tradable assets.

Beneath you lies a medieval village full of people who have no idea they are being watched. They work, marry, raise children, change jobs, commit crimes, worship different gods, fall ill, leave on expeditions and die.

Your task is not to save them. It is to understand them, trade their futures and finish the match with more Souls than your rivals.

You are a god. Mortal lives are stocks.

Every villager is part of a living simulation. Their value depends on health, wealth, career, family, relationships, faith, reputation and recent events.

At the start of each five-year run, you draft villagers and study their dossiers. You can see their family, career, market history, recent events and selected traits. Once the draft is complete, the market opens.

Buy shares in a promising life. Sell before the situation turns bad. Short a villager whose future looks worse than the market believes. Prices respond to events in the village and to the decisions of every player at the table.

A promotion can make someone valuable. A scandal can destroy their reputation. An illness can change the outlook of an entire household. A death closes the market completely.

A village that keeps moving

The simulation does not wait for the players. Villagers work, court one another, marry, have children, inherit property, join churches and cults, fall into debt, commit crimes, face justice and compete for public office.

The village has its own economy, food supply, workplaces, institutions and changing religious balance. Harvests fail. Gangs form. Elections change the government. Families grow old and split apart.

Every run produces different stories. Events are generated by the simulation, and market movements can be traced back to things that happened to real people in the village.

Forecast the future

Before each run, the Fates offer forecasts about the drafted villagers. You may learn about possible death, illness, career changes, family events, volatility and future value.

These forecasts are based on repeated simulations of the same situation. They are useful, but they are not guarantees.

You can also spend Presence to interfere with the lives you are watching. Protect a villager, push them toward a new decision or make their situation worse. Other players may notice that fate was changed, but they will not know who caused it or whether the result was a blessing or a curse.

Asymmetric gods with different strategies

The gods are not interchangeable. Each one has a different cult, starting position, strategic power, military identity and divine intervention.

The current roster includes

  • The Almighty relies on authority, order and miracles.

  • Anubis protects the dead and can return fallen soldiers to the battlefield.

  • Bhaal turns violence, fear and disorder into power.

  • Cthulhu works through madness, dreams and hidden influence.

  • Thor favours direct military strength and heroic trials.

  • Quetzalcoatl uses beauty, creativity and cultural influence.

More gods may join the Divine Exchange in future updates, each bringing new powers, cult mechanics and ways to approach the village.

Choosing a god changes how you approach both the village and the War of Gods. Two players may choose the same god, but their cults, colours, territories, believers and economies remain separate.

Build your cult

Between trading runs, develop your cult and compete for believers. You may lead a lawful church or an illegal cult. Convert households, support priests, manage your treasury and fight for the position of state religion.

Your influence inside the village affects more than faith. It changes elections, public opinion, access to resources and the number of orders available during the War of Gods.

The War of Gods

Between runs, the village clock stops and the game becomes a strategic battle for territory.

Command armies on a territory map. Issue hidden orders, fortify your borders, expand into neutral fields, sabotage rivals and fight for the areas that generate Souls and Presence.

Equip your forces and decide how to spend your limited resources. Expansion, defence, production and sabotage all have a place, but every order creates a risk.

Lose your divine seat and your cult collapses. Hold it, and the village becomes the foundation for your next advantage.

Expeditions and royal levies

Some villagers leave the village on expeditions or royal campaigns. Their journey continues for months and can involve battles, sickness, supply problems, desertion and death.

If anyone returns, the survivors may bring back wealth, influence or other rewards. Players compete in a live auction for the first choice of what comes home.

Features

  • Peer-to-peer multiplayer through Steam Networking

  • 2–10 players with bots available to fill empty seats

  • Draft, buy, sell and short mortal lives

  • A living medieval village simulation

  • Six asymmetric gods with different powers and strategies

  • Cult management, religious influence and public institutions

  • The strategic War of Gods between trading runs

  • Territory control, hidden orders and army equipment

  • Forecasts based on repeated simulations

  • Divine powers that alter villagers’ lives

  • A written chronicle describing the history of the village

  • Four-path skill tree

  • English and Polish localization

  • Save, resume and reconnect during a match

  • Fictional Souls currency only

  • No real-money gambling, cash-out or player-to-player currency trading

store_data.about_the_game:
Eat or be eaten! Survive the endless oceanic struggle for survival!

"Fish World" is a survival action game where you aim to become the ruler of the sea by preying on smaller targets and escaping from massive predators. In this unforgiving food chain where death is always just a bite away, can you reach the top of the "Global Ocean Rankings"?

Eat and Grow! The Ultimate Giant-Killing Action!

The ocean is a world of the survival of the fittest. Touch a fish bigger than you, and it's an instant Game Over! Always keep an eye on your surroundings, and seize the momentary openings to swallow smaller prey whole! The exhilaration of growing large enough to "bite back" at the giant fish you once desperately fled from is the true thrill of this game!

  • Astonishing Evolution Tree:

    Start as the weakest little fish. By continuously feeding, your body will grow massive, transforming you one after another into a mackerel, saury, sea bream, and more!

  • Aim to be the Ruler of the Deep:

    Keep evolving, and you might even turn into that surprising fish!? Satisfy your appetite to reach your final form!

  • Intuitive Action:

    Experience smooth, fluid swimming controls. From split-second dodges to sharp turns that corner your prey, swim through the ocean exactly as you desire!

Swim Through a Beautiful yet Harsh "Ocean World"

As the game progresses, the stage scenery shifts from crystal-clear, bright shallows to the eerie, pitch-black abyss of the deep sea where light cannot reach. Unexpected dangers may lurk in the midground elements drifting in the background, such as seaweed and the shadows of rocks. Read the environmental changes and determine the best route to survive!

◇ Prologue

The Ocean—the cradle of life, and an endless battlefield washed in blood. Behind the seemingly peaceful coral reefs, small lives disappear into the stomachs of predators again today. Massive sharks with overwhelming power, deep-sea fish lurking in the dark... In this sea ruled by unreasonable violence, a single small fish now challenges the absolute hierarchy of the food chain! —Aim for total domination of the Global Ocean!

Other Game Systems

This title incorporates the following systems for a comfortable gameplay experience:

  • Online Ranking Feature

  • Difficulty Adjustment Feature

  • Full Gamepad (Controller) and Keyboard & Mouse Support

  • Achievement System based on your gameplay progress

Regarding Let's Plays & Video Streaming

There are no restrictions on Let's Plays or video streaming! You are welcome to stream the game without needing any special permission. (However, we may contact you if the content contains excessive slander or defamation that damages the image of the work.)

store_data.about_the_game:
Sao Tháng Tám - August Star video game is a First person survival horror game about the Famine that killed nearly 2 million people in Viet Nam in 1945.

In this game, player will experience the main gameplays that the developers hope to accomplish in the full game:

Historical event narration:

Following a tragic journey of the main protagonist on his way to find his lost brother, players will meet with many NPCs, join their stories in the form of side quests to view the full picture of the most disastrous famine in Viet Nam colonial regime history.

[Picture]

Survival horror:

Player will not only have to avoid many realistic enemies like the Japanese colonial soldiers or their henchmen, but also run away from monsters and ghosts that grow from the fears inside the main character.

[Picture]

Stealth action:

Use observational skills and patience to overcome enemies equipped with state-of-the-art weaponry, while avoiding unnecessary casualties to minimize the impact on nearby civilians.

[Picture]

Multiple Endings:

Player's actions and choices in dialogues and quests during the game could lead to multiple bad/good endings.

store_data.about_the_game:
By day you're a shopkeeper. By night you're an explorer.

Run a mysterious antique shop where every object has a story - and some may be better of left undiscovered.

During the day, manage your shop ad turn the treasure you've recovered into profit. Spend your earnings on upgrades, unlock new areas and expand your store into something amazing. Build collections, display rare artifacts and discover what secrets your shop could hold.

When night falls. leave the safety of your shop and venture into dangerous extractions zones in search of valuable antiques and strange objects.

Explore abandoned mansions, mysterious hedge mazes and other dangerous locations, searching furniture, rooms and hidden corners for anything worth bringing home. But you wont have unlimited space. Every item has weight and you'll have to  decide what is worth carrying and what must be left behind.

The deeper you explore, the greater the risk.

And not everything in the extraction zones likes that you're there....

Explore Dangerous Locations 

Venture into abandoned and mysterious locations in search of rare antiques, strange objects and valuable treasures. Search rooms, furniture and hidden corners, but stay alert - you never know what might be lurking nearby. Where will you end up next?

Choose Your Loot

You can't take everything with you. Every item has weight, and your carrying capacity is limited. Do you take the cheap items you know you can carry, or do you risk carrying that rare artifact that could be worth a fortune? 

Build Your Antique Shop

Turn your discoveries into profit and use your earning to expand your shop. Unlock new rooms, improve your abilities and build a store worthy of the treasures you discover. With your shops reputation on the line, you will have to make every night worth the gamble.

Discover and Collect

Not everything you find has to be sold. Discover new items, track them in your collection book and build a collection of rare and unusual artifacts. Display items around your shop (and maybe other places) to gain more standing with the customers buying your wears.

Why Early Access

I am a solo developer working on and creating Oddments & Offerings. The game has only been in development for a few short months, because of this there are a lot of features that still haven't been added to the game yet. Such as more shop expansions, upgrades, new maps, enemies and a whole boat-load of other features I’ll keep a surprise for now!

This game has slowly become my dream project and I am expecting to be working and pushing out updates for the game well after its full release (a long way off yet). As I am making the game solo there is no set date for when the game will be classed as finished but I will be working hard to make sure the experience is as best as it can be.

A short list of intended additions ( VERY ROUGH AND LOTS MORE TO ADD):

  • More maps to explore 

  • Hundreds more items to find and collect

  • Lots more Enemies who are out to get the player

  • Shop Furniture placement and decorating system

  • Museum?

  • Much much more....

The deeper you explore, the greater the risk.

And not everything in the extraction zones likes that you're there....

Explore Dangerous Locations 

Venture into abandoned and mysterious locations in search of rare antiques, strange objects and valuable treasures. Search rooms, furniture and hidden corners, but stay alert - you never know what might be lurking nearby. Where will you end up next?

Choose Your Loot

You can't take everything with you. Every item has weight, and your carrying capacity is limited. Do you take the cheap items you know you can carry, or do you risk carrying that rare artifact that could be worth a fortune? 

Build Your Antique Shop

Turn your discoveries into profit and use your earning to expand your shop. Unlock new rooms, improve your abilities and build a store worthy of the treasures you discover. With your shops reputation on the line, you will have to make every night worth the gamble.

Discover and Collect

Not everything you find has to be sold. Discover new items, track them in your collection book and build a collection of rare and unusual artifacts. Display items around your shop (and maybe other places) to gain more standing with the customers buying your wears.

Why Early Access

I am a solo developer working on and creating Oddments & Offerings. The game has only been in development for a few short months, because of this there are a lot of features that still haven't been added to the game yet. Such as more shop expansions, upgrades, new maps, enemies and a whole boat-load of other features I’ll keep a surprise for now!

This game has slowly become my dream project and I am expecting to be working and pushing out updates for the game well after its full release (a long way off yet). As I am making the game solo there is no set date for when the game will be classed as finished but I will be working hard to make sure the experience is as best as it can be.

A short list of intended additions ( VERY ROUGH AND LOTS MORE TO ADD):

  • More maps to explore 

  • Hundreds more items to find and collect

  • Lots more Enemies who are out to get the player

  • Shop Furniture placement and decorating system

  • Museum?

  • Much much more....

Extract with you're loot, grow your shop and decide what is worth selling - and what is worth keeping.

store_data.about_the_game:
One stroke levels Everest. One sunshade cools the equator.

Most sandboxes treat your brush as paint. Terra Logic hands it to physics. Every stroke feeds a live simulation of climate, ocean and erosion — you are not coloring a planet, you are asking it a question, and it answers with consequences.

You draw. The planet answers.

  • Lower the Tibetan Plateau and the monsoon loses its wall — the rain belts redraw themselves

  • Dam Gibraltar and the Mediterranean dries into a salt desert over centuries; breach it and the Atlantic thunders back in

  • Dig the Sahara's depressions below sea level, let the ocean in, and watch green rim the new shores

  • Pour meltwater into the North Atlantic until the overturning circulation stalls and Europe goes cold — then try to bring it back. It won't come easily: the circulation remembers, and collapse has hysteresis

Not just "what happened" — "why"

Click anywhere on the planet. The causal probe breaks down that spot's temperature and rainfall: how much latitude gives, how much elevation takes, what the currents deliver, and exactly what your edits changed. The simulation is not a black box; every number can be audited.

38 scenarios

Green the Sahara. Reopen the Panama seaway. Breach Gibraltar and refill the Mediterranean. Save the thermohaline circulation. Light six lighthouses on the Moon. Every scenario is a planetary-engineering story worth retelling — Every scenario has a achievable solution; there are no dead ends..

6 star systems

Beyond our own: TRAPPIST-1, Proxima Centauri, TOI-700, Kepler-452, K2-18 — orbits and stellar parameters taken from real observations, sources annotated. Tidally locked worlds run their own climate logic: a day side that never sleeps, a night side of ice, eyeball oceans along the terminator. And one more Earth — the Cretaceous, 90 million years ago, its continents placed by paleogeographic reconstruction.

A quiet workbench

No resource bars. No enemies. No countdown. A muted interface, a whispering narrator, Beethoven and Bach's Goldberg Variations in public-domain recordings. Seven languages: English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, 한국어, Français, Deutsch.

Features

  • Real climate: an energy-balance model drives temperature, ice, rainfall and biomes

  • Three-layer ocean: wind-driven gyres, a thermohaline conveyor that can collapse — and be rescued — and sea-air coupling

  • Conserved water: it flows downhill, and inland seas fill or dry by physics

  • Real erosion: rivers incise, breach and re-route, carved into the heightfield

  • Causal probe and chronicle: every consequence can be questioned and replayed

  • 38 scenarios plus free play on every body

  • The Moon, Mars, Cretaceous Earth and five real exoplanet systems

store_data.about_the_game:
Explore a Beautiful World. A Story of a “Mother” and “Daughter”

“Set forth, Lityria. This is the path you chose—”

In the haze of a shallow sleep, a voice calls her awake.
Is it the voice of her mother—or someone else...?

〇 Explore a Vast World

An exploration-focused RPG that takes you across vast lands, sprawling underground areas, and mysterious labyrinths.
The game features approximately 380 maps to explore.

Use the abilities you acquire to smash rocks, overcome cliffs and elevation changes, move obstacles, and solve mechanisms as you venture deeper into the unknown.

Gain new powers, open new paths, and journey onward to places you have yet to see.

〇 Twelve Labyrinths

Twelve unique labyrinths await you across the world.

At the deepest reaches of each labyrinth stands its master, guarding a mysterious key.

With every labyrinth you conquer, lost memories return—and the true nature of the world slowly begins to reveal itself.

〇 A Journey of Three Companions

Lityria — A quiet, laid-back young woman who rarely shows her emotions.
Theia — A cheerful, quick-witted boy who sometimes seems surprisingly mature for his age.
Selene — A knowledgeable and endlessly curious woman whose idea of “common sense” can be a little unusual.

Travel the world together, sharing moments along the way.

Across the land, you will also meet fellow Explorers, each following their own journey and carrying their own story.

〇 Explore, Gather, Grow Stronger

Each member of the party wields a different weapon, which can be strengthened using materials found throughout the world.

Evolve your weapons with elemental gemstones and continue upgrading them to become stronger.
Take your carefully honed weapon into battle and face powerful foes.

Offer Crystal Stones to Goddess Statues scattered across the world to learn new skills.

Search for even greater abilities, and venture deeper into unexplored lands—

〇 Explore a Beautiful World

Landscapes transform between day and night.

Rain, storms, and blizzards may hinder your journey as you explore the far-reaching surface world and the vast underground realms beneath it.

Set out in search of sights you have never seen and stories you have yet to discover—

〇 Game Features

  • An exploration-focused RPG where you can freely travel across vast 3D environments.

  • Explore diverse regions including grasslands, deserts, wetlands, snowfields, and underground caverns in search of skills, materials, and labyrinths.

  • Acquire new abilities deep within the labyrinths to gradually expand the areas you can explore.

  • A fixed party of three characters, visible enemy encounters, and an Active Turn Battle system.

  • Complete requests from the Explorers’ Guild and rise through its ranks.

  • Follow the journey of three companions as they uncover the “truth of the world.”

store_data.about_the_game:
USE IT UNTIL YOU LOOSE IT

Module Madness is a top-down bullet-hell roguelite about attrition. Every module you scavenge has a durability. Spend it, and the module is gone for good. Kit out your ship from wrecks and supply drops, burn through it in combat, and take whatever survives into the next solar system. Pick a ship, drop in, fight until you die.

MODULES ARE EVERYTHING

Our ship has one cannon, and that is it. Every ability, every bonus sits in the modules you pick up along the way. What you are carrying decides how you play, and no two runs hand you the same set — over 25 modules across five rarity tiers, and more than 150,000 unique combinations of them.

ACTIVE AND PASSIVE

Active modules you trigger yourself: bombs, lasers, shields, dashes. A laser that sweeps in a rotating arc. A dash that cuts through whatever it passes. A minefield you leave behind you. A shield that fires itself when things get tight. Passive modules work quietly in the background, raising values like damage, speed or health, or adding projectiles to your front, sides and rear. How many of each fit on board depends on the ship.

NOTHING LASTS

Every use wears a module down, and passive modules wear out in the background too. Sooner or later they break, and there is nowhere to repair them. The slot sits empty and you move on. So every trigger pull is a decision. Spend the shield now, or hold it for the boss. Burn the legendary module now or save it for later. You are not building toward the perfect loadout, you are working with whatever still fires.

CARGO CONTAINERS

Downed enemies leave containers behind. Open one and it offers you a choice of modules: choose well. Larger containers hold more loot. Whatever you leave behind, you will not see again. Supply drops sit out in the open for anyone willing to go and get them. And when a trader turns up, you can buy, sell and reroll the stock — invest enough and the restricted goods come out from under the counter.

YOU PICK THE ROUTE

Before every section you see what is waiting: enemy types, threat level, expected loot. Safe and lean, or dangerous and worth it.

WHAT IS WAITING

Five enemy types across three tiers each. Hunters that run you down, swarm bots that crowd you out, pattern shooters that spray you down, reflector tanks that throw your own shots back at you. Fights happen in sealed arenas — no running away, no endless kiting, just you, and whatever space you carve out. Every solar system ends with a multi-phase boss.

IT DOES NOT STOP

No time limit. Endless runs. One solar system follows the next, each harder than the last. The run ends when you die. Then the numbers come up: how deep you got, how long you lasted, what you killed, what you banked. Above them sits your best run so far. That is the one you are actually up against.

AT A GLANCE

  • Top-down bullet-hell roguelite built around attrition

  • Modules with durability — using them spends them, and broken means gone

  • 25+ active and passive modules, five rarity tiers, 150,000+ unique combinations

  • Five enemy types in three tiers, plus scaling multi-phase bosses

  • Sealed arenas: no escape

  • Pick your own route with enemy types, threat level and loot shown up front

  • Three unique ships with different Stats

  • Endless runs until you die

  • Mouse and keyboard or controller, Xbox Gamepad Support

Worker 1331

Your task is simple: work and follow the work instructions.

Grab. Split. Load. Deliver.

Pull the handle, get the stumps, split them into pieces and load the logs into the cart. Earn Tickets, buy upgrades and gradually make wood processing faster and more efficient.

Every stump needs to be split. Every log needs to be carried.

Upgrade

Spend the Tickets you earn on equipment upgrades.

Upgrade the splitting heads, install cooling, increase the number of stumps delivered at once, carry more logs and make the manual work easier.

Decide for yourself which upgrades you need.

Work faster or simply make the job easier.

Observe

For fire safety reasons, the stumps are stored in a separate room that you are not allowed to enter. A special mechanism delivers them through a vacuum system of rigid and flexible ducts. You can only observe it through the cameras.

Use the work computer, study the instructions, read the occasional messages, and try to understand what is happening beyond your workplace.

Finish the job

A huge pile of logs.

It will slowly get smaller.

You are Worker 1331.

Just keep working.

store_data.about_the_game:
Wulfrot is First Person Horror Game set in the age of 1315.

It was a hard and desperate time, and belief in the Devil was just as real as belief in God. People whispered about others who had taken the shape of a wolf. Not a curse but a choice made in hunger and blessed by no priest.

Having no other place left to run you return to the village you grew up having no choice but to face what has been hunting you for so many years.


What to expect:

  • Explore a dark and filled with secrets village on foot with no waypoints, no objective markers. Just a torch and a hand-drawn map to guide you.

  • Witness a story built on guilt, silence, and grief, revealed only to those willing to look deep into the abyss.

  • Evade a stalking threat that hunts by sound and light, no scripted patrol routes.

  • Investigate what happened here through what's left behind.

  • Survive desperate encounters. This is not a power fantasy , you are not built to fight back.

  • A first-person, single-player horror experience focused on atmosphere and tension over combat.

I'll keep this page updated as things take form, and share the games progress along the way.

Wishlist WULFROT to follow its development.

store_data.about_the_game:
繁华的都市，生活节奏日益加快，人们的生活压力也越来越大。晚睡，早起，赶地铁，赶公车，赶工，赶着商店的促销……不知不觉中，我们似乎已经习惯了。

但是，我们可能在某个下雨的半夜惊醒，独自一人站在阳台，思考着，这就是我们想要的生活吗？

是的，这个站在阳台，听着雨声滴答，陷入沉思的人就是我。

曾经，我的梦想就是开一家小店，看着来来往往的食客，给他们做一些家乡的美食，听听他们工作生活中的趣闻。如果赚钱我就多雇几个人，不赚钱的话，就自己一个人搞。心情好，我就开门营业，心情不好，就歇业出去旅行。

想着想着，天亮了，雨停了。晨曦的光芒，透过挂在阳台上晾晒的衣服，照到我的脸上，我决定了，辞职。

……

三个月后，依灵餐厅开业了。

依灵餐厅开在公园旁，这里，没有人来人往，没有车水马龙。只有公园林间嬉戏的鸟儿，和路边跳广场舞的阿姨。

餐厅的运行需要雇佣员工，研发菜谱，并确保每个月的收入大于支出，否则，就会有破产的风险。当然，你也可以另辟蹊径，通过倒卖食材赚取更多的收益。

同时，你需要不断的扩建餐厅来应对日益增长的顾客数量。否则你将会因为餐厅经常满座而错过一些客人。

有些客人，错过，可能就不会再见到了。他们都是有故事的人，坐下来，好好听听他们的经历，或许，你们一见如故，他就会留下来和你一起经营餐厅。

随着餐厅的知名度不断上升，你需要参与餐厅星级评选，评选成功后，将会获得更多高级菜谱和解锁更多的员工，并且会增加客流量。

虽然，你可能不喜欢竞争，但餐饮协还是会把你的餐厅和其他餐厅排在一起，分出个123来。但这些都是虚名，我知道你不在意的。

至于依灵餐厅的归宿是什么，我也不知道，还是你去探索吧。
