store_data.about_the_game:
Travel. Survive. Fight. Decide who deserves to stand beside you... in a world where faith can become madness.

A tactical turn-based RPG combined with free-roaming exploration in a dark fantasy world filled with conflict, survival, and difficult choices.

Lead your own caravan across a dangerous land. Explore towns, wilderness, ruins, and forgotten places. Recruit new companions, take on quests, gather resources, and make the choices necessary to keep your people alive.

But combat isn't the only thing you have to worry about.

Food, exhaustion, and stress can gradually wear down your companions. The choices you make can change relationships, shape factions, and determine who becomes an ally — or an enemy.

🗺️ Explore a Hostile World

Lead your caravan and freely travel across a dangerous fantasy world.

Discover towns, villages, ruins, hidden locations, and unexpected events along the way. Take on quests, search for resources, and decide how far you are willing to push your group.

Every journey comes at a cost.

Manage your food supplies, exhaustion, and the mental state of your companions while deciding when to move forward and when to stop and recover.

Sometimes, the safest road isn't the best one.

⚔️ Tactical Turn-Based Combat

When negotiation fails, combat decides the outcome.

Position your companions, choose your targets, use abilities, and take advantage of the battlefield in grid-based tactical combat.

Every character has their own abilities, strengths, and role within the group.

Attack from the flank.
Use high ground to gain an advantage.
Charge into your enemies.
Harness magic and powerful abilities.
Or retreat when the fight is no longer worth the lives it may cost.

Every Action Point matters, and a single mistake can turn the tide of battle.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Build Your Own Band of Travelers

Your party is made up of more than just characters you create yourself.

Hire wandering mercenaries, encounter survivors, and meet characters who can join your group through quests and events.

Each companion has their own abilities, personality, and story.

Someone you save today may become an invaluable member of your party tomorrow.

Or they may have their own reasons for walking away.

🩸 God Sight

There is a cult feared throughout the land.

God Sight.

They believe that humanity can come closer to divine perception by completely shutting away the five senses.

To God Sight, pain is not something to be avoided.

It is a path.

Members of the cult have been found carrying out horrifying rituals. People are taken from their homes, while others willingly submit themselves to the teachings of the faith.

But behind their cruelty lies an even more disturbing question.

Are they truly searching for God — or are they searching for something that was never meant to be found?

⚖️ A World Divided

God Sight is not the only threat.

The world is divided between groups with their own ambitions and beliefs.

  • Villagers and local communities struggling to protect their homes.

  • Soldiers and knights attempting to maintain order.

  • Resistance groups fighting against God Sight.

  • And other factions pursuing their own interests.

As a group of travelers, you don't always have to choose a single side.

Help them.
Deceive them.
Negotiate with them.
Or stay out of their affairs entirely.

The choices you make will determine who you become in this world.

🧠 Survival Is More Than HP

Staying alive isn't simply about keeping your health bar above zero.

Your companions need food.
They need rest.
They suffer from exhaustion.
And they carry the psychological weight of what they experience.

Long battles, losing companions, and traumatic events can affect the mental state of your party.

Because in a world this brutal...

the most dangerous enemy may not be the one standing in front of you, but the one growing inside you.

✦ How Far Will You Take Your Band?

Build your own group of travelers.
Cross a dangerous fantasy world.
Uncover the truth behind God Sight.
Confront competing factions.
And decide for yourself who deserves your help.

Survive the journey.
Fight for what you believe in.
And uncover the truth behind God Sight.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build Your Deck and Reclaim the Lost Constellations


The stars above the Six Academies are going dark, one by one. The names and memories bound to them are vanishing as well.

Choose your Academy, build a 30-card deck, pursue sealed records, and recover scattered memories as you uncover the truth behind the fading stars.

Build a Strategy of Your Own


Choose minions, spells, and weapons from 168 cards available at launch. Create chains of effects around Academy skills, card abilities, and Bonds.

Manage your Mana, board position, and attack timing. Every turn asks you to choose between pressing the attack, protecting a key unit, or preparing for the next round.

Refine decks built around aggression, control, healing, Armor, spell combinations, sacrifice, or Fatigue, then test them against different enemies and Boss mechanics.

Master the Six Academies


Command the Ember, Tide, Gale, Stone, Radiant, and Umbral Academies.

Every Academy features a distinct hero skill, card synergies, and deck-building identity. Master a favorite strategy or expand your collection to explore new Academies and combinations.

Reshape Cards with Startraces


Fuse duplicate cards into a chosen main card and engrave it with permanent Startraces.

Combine Startraces, Bonds, Card Fates, and Boss Imprints to strengthen a card's attributes and tactical abilities. Even an ordinary card can grow throughout your journey and become the heart of your deck.

Challenge the Stolen Memories


Journey through an eight-chapter campaign spanning 60 nodes and confront eight Bosses with unique mechanics and changing phases.

Travel deeper into the Six Academies through card duels, story events, and route choices. Recover sealed records and piece together the memories scattered across the stars.

Each chapter features its own story sequence and Boss encounter. Study the Boss, adjust your deck, and prepare for each phase transition as you pursue the truth behind the Tide of Oblivion.

Raid Supercharged Bosses Together


Enter Co-op Raid with an AI companion or one friend. Each fighter brings their own 30-card deck to face eight supercharged Bosses.

Both players manage their own Health, hand, Mana, and board, taking turns before the Boss phase begins. Watch whether your teammate summoned, cast a spell, attacked, or used an Academy skill, then answer with the right action to trigger a team combo.

Some cards also gain co-op support abilities, allowing you to heal your teammate, grant Armor, and help the party survive the Boss's assaults.

Defeat seven rotating regular Bosses to unlock the final raid target. Clearing the finale opens a new raid cycle with a new rotation.

Conquer Extreme Bosses


Defeat a Co-op Boss on Normal to unlock its Extreme challenge.

Extreme Bosses have more Health, stronger phase mechanics, a faster tempo, and far more dangerous party-wide assaults. Victory demands more than a powerful individual deck—it requires complementary builds and carefully coordinated actions.

Clear an Extreme raid to earn bonus resources and a Boss Trophy Pack for your next challenge.

Choose Your Challenge


Beyond the complete Star Map campaign, several standalone modes await:

  • Roguelike Adventure: Climb through eight floors of randomized trials. Choose routes across three difficulty levels, gain temporary upgrades, and push deeper into each run.
  • Free Battle: Choose any available Academy and deck, then challenge the AI in a standalone duel.
  • Eight Sovereigns: Unlocks after completing the main campaign. Use the same deck to face all eight Bosses in succession while Health carries between battles. Choose one field supply after every victory, with the Boss order changing between runs.
  • Astral Arena: Unlocks after Chapter 1. Pursue seven wins before suffering three losses, face increasingly powerful opponents, and open a rank chest based on your final record.
  • Co-op Raid: Fight supercharged Bosses alongside an AI companion or a friend, using support effects and team combos to complete repeated raid cycles.

Play Together Through Steam or LAN


The full Steam edition supports Steam friend rooms and invitations.

The full game also supports LAN duels and Boss raids. Create a room on the same local network and the game will automatically discover available sessions.

Whether you connect through Steam or LAN, both players can bring their own 30-card decks and face each other in a private one-on-one duel, or form a two-player party and challenge a Boss on Normal or Extreme. No public matchmaking server is required, making it suitable for homes, dorms, and in-person gatherings.

Play at Your Own Pace


Phantom Cardia: Astral Card Duel is a deck-building card game centered on offline single-player content, with additional AI co-op, LAN multiplayer, and Steam friend multiplayer.

The complete campaign, deck progression, and main challenges can be played offline. Even without going online, you can experience the full Co-op Raid rules with an AI companion.

The game is sold as a one-time purchase. Card packs and resources are earned through play, with no forced advertising, paid card pulls, or daily-task pressure.

store_data.about_the_game:
Learn 19×19 Go Through Play

You know the rules. The full board still feels far away. This is a complete beginner’s course for that gap.

Professional player Hibiki-sensei (Kansai Ki-in) and her assistant Kanon walk you through each lesson with portraits, dialogue, and a living 19×19 board.

As you work through the course, the once-baffling 19×19 board will gradually begin to make sense.

Meet Your Teachers

Hibiki-sensei (Hibiki Mishima) Right

A professional Go player affiliated with the Kansai Ki-in, originally from Okayama.

She first discovered Go after happening to pass by the Kansai Ki-in. Nothing makes her happier than seeing more people come to love the game.

During lessons, she explains the essential ideas clearly and guides you in the right direction. During matches, she offers advice based on how the game is unfolding.

Kanon (Kanon Uemura) Left

A 5-dan amateur Go instructor from Kyoto.

She began playing Go in high school and now teaches students of all levels throughout the Kansai region, from complete beginners to dan-level players.

Her teaching emphasizes becoming stronger through understanding while sharing what makes Go so fascinating. During lessons, she asks questions from the student’s perspective. During matches, she plays to win.

Profiles, videos, and photo galleries featuring both instructors are also available as bonus content within the game.

Lectures

From first moves to territory and thickness, joseki, fuseki, strong and weak stones, tesuji, attack and invasion, whole-board judgment, and the endgame. Fourteen sections build the thinking you need for 19×19.

Click to advance the conversation, or answer by choosing a point on the board. Cleared lectures are recorded.

Challenge Matches

Face a slime, goblin, orc, dragon, and demon king — then the teachers themselves — on a full 19×19 board.

Handicap games from 9 stones down to even. Opponents react to the position as you play.

The engine is KataGo, bundled with the game. No extra install.

A win-rate bar, 3-move assist, and territory prediction can be toggled during play. After the game: review, save the record, or show a QR code.

Problems, Joseki, Proverbs

  • Problems

  • Joseki Dictionary — Review joseki with accompanying explanations.

  • Go Proverbs — Collect proverbs and learn what they mean through board examples.

Extras

Teacher profiles, videos, and a photo gallery. Unlock them with points earned in challenge matches.

For players who

  • Know the rules but don’t know what to think about on 19×19

  • Can play 9×9 but haven’t found their footing on the full board

  • Prefer conversation and demonstration over a textbook

  • Want to study Go but find it difficult to begin with books

【Cozy Greenhouse Organization Simulator】

You bought an abandoned greenhouse.

Sort and arrange 2597 flowers and plants, put everything in its proper place, and turn the neglected greenhouse into the garden of your dreams.

【Bring the Greenhouse Back to Life】

  • Sort & Organize: From colorful flowers to all kinds of plants, use their names, colors, species, and other clues to figure out where each one belongs.

  • A Greenhouse Full of Plants: What looks overwhelming at first slowly starts to come together. Organize every flower and plant, fill the empty spaces, and watch the greenhouse take shape piece by piece.

【Make the Greenhouse Yours】

  • Clean Up the Mess: The greenhouse has seen better days. Pick up scattered pots and plants, sort everything out, and slowly turn the neglected space into a cozy, organized greenhouse.

  • Organize Your Way: Decide how you want to tackle the greenhouse. Find the route and rhythm that work best for you as you carry, sort, and arrange your plants.

  • Compete for the Top Spot: Found the fastest way to organize everything? Compare your best time with other players and climb the online leaderboard.

【Helpful Skills】

As you progress, you’ll unlock skills that make organizing the greenhouse easier and faster.

  • Gather: Quickly bring matching flowers or plants directly to you, saving you the trouble of searching around the greenhouse.

  • Spotlight: Highlights matching plants, making them much easier to find among all the pots and flowers.

  • Auto-Place: Automatically places the plants you’re carrying into their correct spots, helping you organize the greenhouse even faster.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to Lock 87

You took this job to earn your way out, but every shift gives them more time to find you.

1992. East Grindle District.

Desperate to earn enough for a black-market visa, you accept a job with the Central Canal Authority and are assigned to Lock 87: an isolated checkpoint where cargo vessels pass between districts under the watch of a brutal regime.

The work is simple: Check the documents. Follow the regulations. Operate the lock. Get paid.

Compliance is mandatory.

CONTROL THE CHECKPOINT

When a vessel requests passage, its documents are delivered through a slot in the bunker wall.

Examine permits, cargo declarations, itineraries and vessel records against an ever-changing set of regulations. Investigate discrepancies, approve legitimate traffic and deny anything that doesn't belong.

Once cleared, operate the lock's industrial controls yourself, opening gates and adjusting the water level to send each vessel on its way.

Inaccuracy and lenience are not advised.

KEEP THE LIGHTS ON

Lock 87 depends on an ageing generator.

Keep it fuelled and running to power your lights, security systems and lock controls. If it fails, the bunker is plunged into darkness and the machinery around you falls silent.

You will then be required to leave the safety of the control room and restore power manually.

WATCH YOUR SURROUNDINGS

The Central Canal Authority has determined that Lock 87 can be safely and efficiently operated by a single employee.

You are alone at your post.

There is no need for concern.

Your only contact with the outside world comes through a radio and fax machine. A narrow window overlooks the lock chamber, while a network of CCTV cameras provides your only view of the surrounding facility.

As the shifts pass, the rules become harder to follow, the machinery less reliable, and the feeling that you are being watched becomes harder to ignore.

EARN YOUR ESCAPE

Every completed shift brings you closer leaving East Grindle behind.

It also gives them another night to find you.

Can you earn enough to escape the district before it's too late?

store_data.about_the_game:
You build it. Then you have to drive it.

CrashFest is an arcade racer that never hands you a circuit. You snap one together out of hairpins, ramps, helixes and holes — and then the whole field races it for points, everybody bolts on one more piece, and you race it again.

By round five the track is three times the length, four people have left mines on it, and that lovely chicane you were so pleased with is the exact reason you are last.

No level select. No track designers. Just whatever six drivers thought was a good idea at the time.

Everyone gets a turn with the track

  • 27 snap-together pieces — hairpins, sweepers, chicanes, banked curves, ramps, four helixes, and five with holes straight through the road

  • One piece per racer, per round, handed out in finishing order

  • The bots build too. They pick at random, which is exactly as dangerous as it sounds

  • Start from nothing if you like — an empty grid and a field laying the first circuit together

  • Save a track you are proud of and bring it back another night

Racing, with the gloves off

  • Seven power-ups — shotgun, landmine, barrier, tyre stack, tow line, shield and a homing missile that picks its own target

  • A wreck is not the end of your round. You wait at the next gate as a ghost and rejoin the moment a survivor reaches it

  • Get left behind far enough that the camera cannot hold you and you are gone. Keep up

  • Dropped hazards are permanent. Mines and barriers outlive the round, so by round four the track is visibly a place where four races have already happened

  • Armco down both edges — or switch it off, and a mistake costs you the race instead of a tenth

Three ways to play with no track at all

  • SUMO — six cars on a rooftop with no parapet and a hole in the middle. Last one still up there wins

  • BOMB TAG — walled roof, one bomb, one fuse. Touch somebody to hand it on. The fuse does not reset

  • TURF — the floor is carved into a slice each and there is one ball. Every second it sits in your slice, you score. Nobody is ever eliminated

On one screen, on one sofa

  • Six cars on the grid — friends and bots come out of the same six seats

  • Bots yield. Somebody picking up a controller is never told the race is full

  • Up to four gamepads, Xbox and PlayStation both mapped properly, with keyboard blocks for anyone left over

  • Pick your colour and your name — the lobby remembers both

  • A match runs to a points target: around a quarter of an hour, five rounds, and a track that grows the whole way through

  • One piece per racer, per round, handed out in finishing order

  • The bots build too. They pick at random, which is exactly as dangerous as it sounds

  • Start from nothing if you like — an empty grid and a field laying the first circuit together

  • Save a track you are proud of and bring it back another night

Racing, with the gloves off

  • Seven power-ups — shotgun, landmine, barrier, tyre stack, tow line, shield and a homing missile that picks its own target

  • A wreck is not the end of your round. You wait at the next gate as a ghost and rejoin the moment a survivor reaches it

  • Get left behind far enough that the camera cannot hold you and you are gone. Keep up

  • Dropped hazards are permanent. Mines and barriers outlive the round, so by round four the track is visibly a place where four races have already happened

  • Armco down both edges — or switch it off, and a mistake costs you the race instead of a tenth

Three ways to play with no track at all

  • SUMO — six cars on a rooftop with no parapet and a hole in the middle. Last one still up there wins

  • BOMB TAG — walled roof, one bomb, one fuse. Touch somebody to hand it on. The fuse does not reset

  • TURF — the floor is carved into a slice each and there is one ball. Every second it sits in your slice, you score. Nobody is ever eliminated

On one screen, on one sofa

  • Six cars on the grid — friends and bots come out of the same six seats

  • Bots yield. Somebody picking up a controller is never told the race is full

  • Up to four gamepads, Xbox and PlayStation both mapped properly, with keyboard blocks for anyone left over

  • Pick your colour and your name — the lobby remembers both

  • A match runs to a points target: around a quarter of an hour, five rounds, and a track that grows the whole way through
store_data.short_description: Build the track, then race it. Everyone adds a piece between rounds — the bots too — so the corner that just wrecked you is somebody's fault. Local arcade racing for up to six, with shotguns, landmines and homing missiles, plus three arena modes for when you want the track gone.

Hold the pass. Guard the realm.

The dark army marches on Wardstone, and only your towers stand between it and the last free hold. Line the winding roads with archers, knights, mages and siege engines, call down meteors and firestorms, and send a champion into the thick of the fight. Every wave is a puzzle; every road, a killing field of your own design.

Build a killing field

  • Six tower families — precise archers, frontline barracks, arcane mages, thunderous artillery, gold-spinning mines and warding control towers — each with three tiers and four branching specializations.
  • Heroes — lead a champion with a signature ability, from rallying warhorns to earth-shattering strikes, and grow them stronger through the campaign.
  • Battle spells — Meteor, Firestorm, Frost Nova, Reinforcements and Powder Barrels, ready at the tap of a button.

Chain reactions, devastating payoffs

Set up combos and watch them cascade — shatter frozen foes, overload the conductive, and drive the chain toward a screen-clearing Resonance Burst. Control sets up the payoff; timing lands it.

A realm worth defending

  • Towering bosses — face the Drowned King, the Mire Colossus and other hand-drawn horrors that shrug off everything you throw at them.
  • Ward Sigils & Blight — optional modifiers that reshape a battle for greater rewards.
  • Trials, Boss Rush and Endless — when the campaign is won, the real challenge begins.

Made to be mastered

  • 55 distinct foes with real counter-play — armor, magic resistance, swarms, healers and ward-breakers.
  • Target priorities, veteran towers, and an economy that rewards bold, aggressive play.
  • Fully localized in 14 languages.

store_data.about_the_game:
Master the Challenge

GameOvrd2 is a retro-inspired precision platformer built around fast reactions, careful movement, pattern recognition, consistency, and the satisfaction of gradually mastering increasingly demanding challenges. Navigate a handcrafted collection of levels packed with deadly traps, unexpected hazards, chaotic encounters, deceptive obstacles, and carefully placed surprises designed to keep you constantly reconsidering what might be waiting just beyond the next screen.

Every level introduces its own combination of platforming challenges and environmental threats, requiring you to observe, adapt, experiment, and ultimately master the mechanics standing between you and the finish. What initially appears straightforward can quickly become considerably more dangerous as familiar ideas are rearranged, combined, and pushed into increasingly demanding situations.

Nothing Is Random

Nothing is random. Enemy behavior, hazards, traps, boss attacks, and other gameplay elements follow consistent and predictable rules. If something kills you, you can learn it. If you can learn it, you can anticipate it. And if you can anticipate it, you can eventually execute it faster.

Built for Speedrunning

That predictability makes GameOvrd2 particularly well suited to speedrunning. Levels aren't designed around waiting for favorable random outcomes or hoping that an encounter behaves the way you need it to. Improvement comes from learning patterns, discovering more efficient routes, refining movement, reducing hesitation, and executing increasingly precise strategies. A run can be practiced, repeated, optimized, and pushed further as your understanding of the game improves.

Learn. Adapt. Try Again.

Expect narrow escapes, mistimed jumps, sudden deaths, repeated attempts, and those wonderfully frustrating moments where success was only a fraction of a second away. Learn from each failure, refine your approach, develop the muscle memory needed to overcome difficult sequences, and push forward through a deliberately constructed progression of challenges that rewards persistence and precision.

Completion Is Only the Beginning

For players interested in mastery, completing a level is only the beginning. Familiar sections can gradually become opportunities for optimization as unnecessary movements disappear, difficult sequences become automatic, and previously intimidating encounters turn into rehearsed patterns. Whether you're simply trying to survive or attempting to shave another few seconds off a run, the underlying game remains consistent: the challenge doesn't change between attempts—you do.

Face What Comes Next

Along the way, survive chaotic encounters, uncover unexpected twists, overcome increasingly elaborate obstacles, and face unforgettable boss fights that put everything you have learned to the test. GameOvrd2 combines the immediacy and simplicity of classic platformers with modern precision-focused gameplay to create an experience centered on challenge, discovery, repetition, optimization, and eventual mastery.

store_data.about_the_game:
Everyone else wants you out


SIDE OUT is a last-side-standing arena game. You hold one edge of a polygon, the ball comes at you, and if it gets past you it costs you a life. You get two. There is nothing to unlock and nothing to read, which is the point, because by the time you have finished wondering what the controls are you have already lost one of them.

Getting knocked out is not the end of your round


Dead players become saboteurs. You drop bumpers, warps and spinners into the arena, then watch the survivors try to read a board that keeps changing. Nobody sits out watching a round they were eliminated from. You just switch sides.

The arena eats itself


Every knockout takes a wall out of the world. Eight sides become six, then four, and the last two players end up staring at each other across a shape with nowhere left to hide. At 75 seconds a second ball joins in, then another every 34 seconds, up to six at once.

Modes


  • CLASSIC. Eight players, one polygon, last side standing.
  • ARENA. Up to twenty players around a ring of obstacles.
  • PRIVATE ROOM. Send a link, play with exactly who you want.
  • SOLO. Practice offline against bots.

Your friends do not need Steam


SIDE OUT is one game across every screen it runs on. The Steam version shares its rooms with players on the web and on phones. Same arena, same round, same clock. Send an invite to anyone, on anything.

No waiting


  • Bots fill any empty side instantly, so a round never waits for a full room.
  • Walk in mid-match and you take a bot's place on the spot.
  • Rounds end in a minute or two.

Explore the unknown depths with adorable robots!


Deep Sea Survivor is a pixel-art survival game that combines bullet heaven action with roguelite exploration.

Defeat swarms of sea creatures, overcome dangerous traps, and dive deeper into the ocean. Instead of fighting inside a single open arena, explore stages featuring varied layouts, terrain, hazards, and paths.

Simple Controls, Satisfying Survival Action


All you need to control your robot is directional movement and a dash. It is easy to pick up, but survival depends on reading enemy movements, avoiding traps, and dashing at the right moment.

Create Your Build from Three Choices


Whenever you level up, choose one of three options to acquire a new skill or strengthen one you already have. Every run develops differently depending on the weapons and upgrades you select.

Collect Robots with Unique Starting Skills


Each robot begins with a different signature skill. Collect new robots and discover the weapons and upgrades that best complement their abilities.

Explore, Gather Resources, and Upgrade Your Gear


Search each stage for resources used to strengthen your equipment. Decide whether to risk exploring dangerous areas for valuable materials or take a safer path toward survival.

A Different Journey into the Depths


The deeper you dive, the more varied the terrain becomes—and the deadlier the traps and sea creatures waiting for you. Explore diverse maps, discover new combinations, and survive your journey to the deepest reaches of the ocean!

  • Simple directional movement and dash controls
  • Choose one of three upgrades whenever you level up
  • Collect adorable robots with different starting skills
  • Explore maps with varied layouts, terrain, and traps
  • Gather resources to strengthen your equipment
  • Create a different roguelite build on every run
  • Battle cute and distinctive pixel-art sea creatures

Whenever you level up, choose one of three options to acquire a new skill or strengthen one you already have. Every run develops differently depending on the weapons and upgrades you select.

Collect Robots with Unique Starting Skills


Each robot begins with a different signature skill. Collect new robots and discover the weapons and upgrades that best complement their abilities.

Explore, Gather Resources, and Upgrade Your Gear


Search each stage for resources used to strengthen your equipment. Decide whether to risk exploring dangerous areas for valuable materials or take a safer path toward survival.

A Different Journey into the Depths


The deeper you dive, the more varied the terrain becomes—and the deadlier the traps and sea creatures waiting for you. Explore diverse maps, discover new combinations, and survive your journey to the deepest reaches of the ocean!

  • Simple directional movement and dash controls
  • Choose one of three upgrades whenever you level up
  • Collect adorable robots with different starting skills
  • Explore maps with varied layouts, terrain, and traps
  • Gather resources to strengthen your equipment
  • Create a different roguelite build on every run
  • Battle cute and distinctive pixel-art sea creatures
